item.title: 60 Minutes Producers Avoided Michigan Senate Segment Amid Concerns Over Bari Weiss' Influence
item.description: Several producers at '60 Minutes' declined a high-profile assignment involving Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed due to concerns about potential interference from CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss, according to a report by the media newsletter Status. The assignment was ultimately given to Keith Sharman, a producer who frequently collaborates with Norah O'Donnell, following an internal memo that elevated Sharman to senior broadcast producer after a veteran producer retired. The interview with El-Sayed had been in doubt after CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford posted on X (formerly Twitter) supporting a GOP activist's push for El-Sayed to denounce the Muslim Brotherhood, a post she later deleted and apologized for. Network executives debated disciplinary action, but Weiss blocked any serious punishment, deeming the apology sufficient. El-Sayed's campaign had previously expressed frustration with CBS News over a story that highlighted him on the anniversary of 9/11,

item.title: Nostalgic 1950s and 1960s Halloween Costumes Capture Childhood Traditions
item.description: These mid-century photographs from the 1950s and 1960s showcase children dressed in Halloween costumes, reflecting the era's simpler, often handmade fashion. The images depict kids in a variety of outfits, including ghosts, witches, pirates, clowns, skeletons, and popular characters of the time, posing proudly before heading out for trick-or-treating or Halloween parties. Many of the costumes were crafted at home, showcasing the creativity and charm of the period. The photos offer a warm, nostalgic glimpse into childhood Halloween celebrations more than half a century ago, highlighting how traditions and styles have evolved over time. The collection provides a visual narrative of community and family traditions during a time when Halloween was celebrated with a focus on handmade decorations and costumes rather than commercialized themes. These images serve as a historical snapshot of how children engaged with the holiday, emphasizing the importance of personal creativity and community

item.title: Deputy Chief of Staff Accused of Extortion and Court Influence Scheme Linked to Custody Battle
item.description: A lawsuit filed in the Southern District of New York has accused Rafi Silberberg, Deputy Chief of Staff to Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY), along with two other individuals, of orchestrating an extortion and 'court-fixing' scheme targeting Shmuel Goldenberg. According to the complaint, the trio allegedly conspired to influence the outcome of a contentious custody battle involving Goldenberg, demanding extreme measures including the surrender of his home and over $300,000 in child support payments. The lawsuit also alleges that a $50,000 bribe was to be paid directly to Justice Sherri L. Eisenpress, a Rockland County judge who resigned earlier this year following a misconduct investigation. The investigation revealed that Eisenpress had presided over more than 50 cases where she had personal connections to the attorneys involved. The complaint, reported by Kate Lisa of City & State New York, details the alleged scheme as part of a broader pattern of misconduct. The case highlights concerns abou

item.title: NUS Develops First Touchscreen-Integrated Garment with Washable, Flexible Display
item.description: Researchers at the National University of Singapore's College of Design and Engineering have created the world's first touchscreen integrated into a garment. The innovative technology involves threading a fiber that functions as both pixels and touch sensors, allowing the garment to display images and video, respond to touch, and connect wirelessly to digital devices. The sleeve prototype, featuring 54 pixel fibers each containing 96 LEDs, forms a 96 by 54-pixel display measuring 168 mm by 105 mm with 8-bit color depth and 30 frames per second refresh rate. This groundbreaking development overcomes previous limitations of textile-based displays by using a novel interconnection architecture and thermal fiber drawing process that integrates thousands of microelectronic devices along a single fiber. The display remains washable, breathable, and flexible after 50 detergent washes and 1,000 bends around a 5 mm radius, maintaining nearly identical light output and touch response. The technol

item.title: Trump insults reporter over appearance during rally question, sparking social media backlash
item.description: President Donald Trump confronted a Reuters reporter on Thursday afternoon after the journalist questioned why he was canceling some of his rallies for battleground Senate races in red states. Trump's response was aggressive, calling the reporter 'a sick guy' and criticizing his physical appearance, stating, 'Look at this guy. You’re way out of shape. You are disgusting! Put yourself in shape! You look like hell.' The president's outburst quickly drew mockery and criticism on social media. Commenters highlighted the irony of Trump's remarks given his own public image, with one user noting, 'Trump telling someone they look like hell while standing there looking like a microwaved pumpkin is absolutely hilarious.' Another political strategist observed, 'Trump is fat. He’s sweating. His tanner is running down his face. And literally can’t take the easiest softball question.' item.title: CNN’s Jake Tapper Mocks Trump’s Outburst at Reporter Over Kansas Rally Cancellation
item.description: CNN anchor Jake Tapper delivered a sarcastic commentary following President Donald Trump's heated exchange with a reporter regarding his decision to cancel a campaign event in Kansas. The incident occurred after Trump was questioned about abandoning plans to hold a rally with Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is competing in a challenging reelection campaign. When pressed about his health, Trump responded with an aggressive remark, telling the reporter, 'You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.' Tapper, upon replaying the footage in the CNN studio, quipped, 'Classy as always,' and added, 'There should be a reverse-angle camera so I know who he’s talking about.' The White House later stated that Trump would instead participate in over 20 telephone rallies before Election Day to engage more voters, a claim Tapper questioned, saying, 'I’m not sure I buy it.' item.title: Historian notes declining MAGA influence as Fox News ratings drop and GOP figures endorse Democrats
item.description:
Historian Heather Cox Richardson argues in her latest 'Letters from an American' newsletter that the MAGA movement is showing signs of weakening domestically. She cites several recent developments to support her analysis. First, she references a Status report indicating Fox News' October ratings have dropped 27 percent in total viewers and 32 percent among viewers aged 25 to 54 compared to last year, while MS NOW and CNN are experiencing growth. Richardson also reports on The Independent's findings that Trump merchandise stores are closing nationwide, with one owner stating the store had 'run its course.'
The historian highlights instances of Republicans backing Democratic candidates, including Texas Democrat James Talarico's campaign airing ads featuring five former GOP officials urging votes for him over Republican Ken Paxton. item.title: Simba SC Coach Steve Barker Addresses Challenges of CAF Champions League Group Stage Against Cameroonian Team Colombe Sportive
item.description: Simba SC coach Steve Barker has addressed the challenges posed by the CAF Champions League group stage, particularly focusing on the threat presented by Cameroonian newcomers Colombe Sportive. While acknowledging the established names in the group, Barker emphasized that every team presents unique challenges, and Simba must navigate these obstacles to fulfill their continental ambitions this season. The coach highlighted that Colombe Sportive, as a newcomer to the Champions League from Cameroon, will be a significant challenge, stating, 'It's going to be a very challenging group for us, but if you want to reach the far end of such tournaments, you have to get through the group stages regardless of the opposition that you have.' The objective for the Tanzanian side is clear: secure a top-two finish to advance into the latter stages of the competition. item.title: FBI Agents Express Concern Over Potential Federal Law Violations in Election Security
item.description: The article details a concerning development involving FBI agents who have reportedly expressed fears that they may be ordered to illegally seize voting machines or ballots in the upcoming election, potentially violating federal law. The agents are particularly worried about the 1865 law that prohibits federal officials from entering polling places armed, which carries penalties of up to five years in prison and a lifetime ban from federal employment. This concern stems from recent actions by the Trump administration, including a raid on Georgia election offices in January 2023, which was conducted under the direction of Tulsi Gabbard, then Director of National Intelligence, and based on claims from election denier Kurt Olsen. The raid, which involved over 600 boxes of ballots, was justified by a warrant obtained through fabricated claims about Dominion voting machines being controlled from Venezuela—a theory that has been debunked. item.title: Pirro aide admits error in case tied to Trump's political agenda
item.description: A top aide to U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro was recorded admitting a significant error in a case involving former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, who were charged with lying to Congress about their knowledge of an investigation into Hunter Biden's laptop. The incident came to light during a court hearing where FBI agent Bryan Witt testified about a phone call between Pirro's office and House Judiciary Committee counsel Steve Castor. During the call, Carlton Davis, a special counsel in Pirro's office, reportedly said, 'this is our f--- up,' according to Witt's testimony. The case originated from a directive by Kash Patel, a former Trump administration official, who instructed the FBI to examine certain individuals, including Floris, following President Trump's public accusations against 'rogue bureaucrats' for allegedly hiding information about Chinese election interference. item.title: Federal Judge's Critique Highlights DOJ Credibility Crisis Amid Trump Administration
item.description: A federal judge's sharp criticism of the Justice Department's handling of a dispute over the East Potomac Golf Course has sparked concern among legal experts about the department's credibility. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a pointed opinion questioning the Department of Justice's (DOJ) conflicting statements regarding the closure of the golf course, which directly contradicted President Donald Trump's public announcement of a November 15 closure date. The judge's inquiry, 'So who do I believe? Do I believe the President of the United States, or do I believe you?', underscored the growing tension between the executive branch and the judiciary. Former federal prosecutor Harry Litman, writing in his Substack 'Talking Feds,' described Judge Reyes's opinion as a 'frontal attack on the credibility of the entire Department of Justice.' item.title: Jezebel removes over 100 articles with explicit headlines, sparking backlash from former employees
item.description: Jezebel, a women-focused website that launched in 2007 and became known for its edgy and often transgressive feminist content, has removed more than 100 articles from its website. The articles, many of which had sexually explicit or vulgar headlines, now display '404 error' messages. According to a Washington Post review, the publisher stated that the articles were not deleted but temporarily unpublished. The move has caused significant outrage among former staff members, who expressed frustration over the removal of content that was part of the site's identity. The website, which has been a staple of feminist internet culture for nearly two decades, has faced criticism for its decision to take down articles that featured bold and provocative headlines. The publisher's explanation that the content was temporarily unpublished rather than permanently deleted has not quelled the backlash. item.title: Trump receives high-level military briefing amid consideration of renewed Iran strikes
item.description: President Donald Trump received a high-level military briefing on Thursday as his administration evaluates the possibility of launching another major military campaign against Iran, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. Admiral Brad Cooper, the top U.S. commander in the Middle East, made a rare in-person visit to the White House to discuss potential military operations, joining Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine. The meeting, which also addressed other topics, occurred as the U.S. weighs 'resuming major combat operations,' the Journal reported. This comes after a separate White House meeting the previous day involving military leaders and Vice President JD Vance, who has reportedly sought to engage with one of Iran's most influential hard-liners to revive peace negotiations. item.title: Trump makes controversial remarks about Black and Jewish voters in South Carolina rally
item.description: President Donald Trump's recent remarks at a South Carolina rally have drawn significant criticism for their inflammatory nature. During a campaign event supporting Senator Darline Graham's re-election bid for her late brother's Senate seat, Trump unexpectedly addressed races in Michigan and Texas. His comments targeted Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, stating, 'If you're Black or Jewish and if you vote for Abdul, you're crazy – you're crazy,' adding, 'You're crazy anyway.' The remarks sparked immediate backlash on social media, with many users questioning the appropriateness of his comments. Writer Joel Klebanoff commented, 'Calling people crazy is a great way to win them over. For sure,' while noting that Trump's remarks appeared to target Black and Jewish voters regardless of their voting choices. item.title: Ex-Trump aide claims GOP distorts Obama's joke to avoid criticism of Trump's authoritarian tendencies
item.description: Sarah Matthews, a former deputy press secretary in President Donald Trump's first White House who resigned over the January 6 attack, has criticized Republicans for focusing on a superficial aspect of a recent Barack Obama joke while ignoring its more pointed criticism. During an appearance on CNN's 'The Arena,' Matthews explained that the GOP has latched onto Obama's reference to Trump's White House renovations resembling a Cheesecake Factory, using it to paint Democrats as out-of-touch elitists. However, she argued that the real sting of the joke came from Obama's comparison of Trump to Saddam Hussein, highlighting what she described as Trump's authoritarian behavior and the corruption surrounding his administration and family. Matthews emphasized that Trump prioritizes decorating the White House over addressing the economic challenges faced by ordinary Americans. item.title: Justice Department argues compliance with court order on golf course tree removal is 'nearly impossible'
item.description: The Justice Department has informed a federal judge that it is 'nearly impossible' to enforce a court order halting tree clearing at a Washington golf course that President Donald Trump aims to renovate. In a motion filed Thursday, government attorneys requested U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes to pause her October 26 injunction while the administration appeals to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit. The motion asks the judge to rule by November 4. Judge Reyes's order prohibits the Interior Department and the National Park Service from cutting additional trees in East Potomac Park, where Trump has pledged to rebuild a public golf course. The government's motion argues that the requirement to notify the court 'without delay' if anyone seeks to alter the park makes compliance 'nearly impossible' and risks sanctions for any failure. item.title: FBI Used Paid Informant to Develop ISIS Plot With Autistic Teen After Dropping Previous Case
item.description: The FBI has been accused of manufacturing an ISIS-inspired attack plot involving an autistic teenager, Abdullah Ezzeldin Taha Mohamed Hassan, by using a paid informant to groom him. According to a motion filed in federal court, the FBI waited until Hassan turned 18 to deploy the informant, three days after his 18th birthday, following the dismissal of a previous case against him. The motion states that the FBI had previously determined Hassan posed no threat when he was 16, and Virginia prosecutors dropped the case in August 2023. The informant, a non-U.S. citizen with a history of felony drug convictions and a pending deportation order, was paid $329,389.18 by the FBI, including $15,000 for the period of the operation. The informant, who was seeking immigration benefits, was instructed to befriend Hassan online and send him FBI-produced propaganda, including a 'CTHS approved bayah video' used to pledge allegiance to ISIS. item.title: Caravan Destroyed in Deliberate Fire on Portland; Two Arrested for Arson
item.description: A caravan was destroyed in a fire that police believe was started deliberately on Yeats Road in Portland, near the Portland Heights Hotel, around 1 a.m. on October 29. Dorset Police responded to the scene to assist the fire service. The incident is being treated as arson, with a 36-year-old woman from Portland and a 34-year-old man from Weymouth arrested on suspicion of arson with intent to endanger life. Both remain in police custody. Detective Sergeant Simon Austin of Dorset County CID emphasized the need for public assistance, urging anyone who witnessed suspicious activity or captured relevant CCTV or dashcam footage to contact authorities. Police have provided contact details for reporting information, including an online portal and the phone number 101, with occurrence number 55260169390. item.title: Trump confronts reporter over health inquiry during airport press briefing
item.description: President Donald Trump engaged in a heated exchange with Reuters White House correspondent Jacob Bogage during an airport press gaggle on Thursday, shortly after canceling a campaign event. The confrontation occurred as Trump was returning to the White House for a Halloween event, following a canceled rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina. Bogage had previously posted an unflattering close-up photo of Trump on X after the president left for the rally. When asked about his health during the brief press gathering, Trump became visibly agitated, calling Bogage 'sick' and 'disgusting' before abruptly ending the session. The president insisted he was 'feeling perfect' and accused the reporter of being 'out of shape' and looking 'like hell.' Trump also criticized Reuters as 'terrible' and dismissed the question about his travel schedule, stating he was 'going to Florida tomorrow' instead of Kansas, where a rally for Senator Roger Marshall had been canceled. item.title: Barbara Barrie, Oscar and Tony-Nominated Actress, Dies at 95 After Advocating for Medical Aid in Dying Law
item.description: Barbara Barrie, an acclaimed actress nominated for both an Academy Award and a Tony Award, has died at the age of 95. Her daughter, Jane Harnick, and her agent confirmed her passing on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at her Manhattan home. The death was medically assisted following a terminal cancer diagnosis, in compliance with New York State's Medical Aid in Dying Law, a law Barrie had actively supported. Barrie's career spanned over six decades, with notable roles in film, television, and Broadway. She received an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress for her role as Evelyn Stohler in 'Breaking Away' (1979) and an Emmy nomination for the 1980 TV adaptation. Her early career included a Cannes Film Festival Best Actress win for 'One Potato, Two Potato' (1964). On Broadway, she originated the role of Sarah in Stephen Sondheim's 'Company' (1970), earning a Tony nomination. She was widely recognized for her roles as Elizabeth Miller on 'Barney Miller' and 'Nana' Keane on 'Suddenly Su

item.title: Democrats grapple with impeachment strategy amid public pressure to hold Trump accountable
item.description: The article examines the growing tension within the Democratic Party regarding impeachment efforts against President Donald Trump in his second term. While over half of American voters believe Trump has committed impeachable offenses, Democratic leaders remain divided on whether to pursue a third impeachment. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has repeatedly stated they 'haven't ruled anything in, and we haven't ruled anything out,' reflecting the party's cautious approach. Several Democrats, including Rep. John Larson and Rep. Shri Thanedar, have introduced impeachment articles against Trump, but most have lost their primaries due to their stance. The article details numerous allegations against Trump, including accepting luxury jets from Qatar, taking $2 billion from the UAE for a cryptocurrency venture, exchanging pardons for political contributions, and steering federal loans to family and friends. item.description: Rep. Tim Burchett (R-TN), a staunch Trump ally and Tennessee Republican, has indicated he will not step aside for another high-profile Republican seeking a Senate appointment, potentially setting up a significant clash within the MAGA faction. According to the Washington Examiner, citing Punchbowl News, Burchett stated he plans to campaign for the Senate seat even if Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who is running for governor, selects someone else to replace her. Blackburn, who intends to remain in the Senate until sworn in as governor, has not publicly named her preferred successor. The potential appointment has drawn interest from several figures, including Pete Hegseth, the former Trump Pentagon chief who moved to Tennessee in 2022. item.title: Senator Murphy Warns of Trump's Post-Midterm Military Escalation Plan
item.description: Senator Chris Murphy (D-CT) has raised concerns about a military strategy reportedly being developed by the Trump administration for potential action against Iran following the 2026 midterm elections. Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, stated in a post on X that he had been briefed on the plan and described it as 'insane,' arguing it would undermine the United States' commitment to the rule of law and prolong the conflict with Iran. According to Murphy, the plan, which has reportedly been requested by President Trump, may involve targeting civilian infrastructure, a move that could significantly escalate tensions in the Middle East. The senator emphasized that while officials have been asked to develop the strategy, he believes it would not achieve its intended objectives and would instead lead to a cycle of further escalation. item.title: Elections expert dismisses Trump administration's midterm interference claims as ineffective
item.description: David Becker, a former Justice Department attorney and director of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, has criticized President Donald Trump's administration for its attempts to interfere in the upcoming midterm elections. Becker, speaking to Mother Jones, described the administration's efforts as 'a lot of noise' that is failing to achieve its goals. He highlighted several court decisions that have blocked administration initiatives, including an attempt to force California officials to set aside thousands of ballots from alleged noncitizens. Becker noted that the administration has lost 27 out of 27 lawsuits related to voter data, with nine of those courts presided over by Trump-appointed judges. He also addressed concerns about immigration agents appearing at polling places, suggesting that the mere threat of such presence could deter voters from participating, even if agents are not actually deployed. item.title: Virginia Governor Spanberger's Diverse Cabinet Photo Sparks Conservative Backlash
item.description: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger (D-VA) faced significant backlash from MAGA influencers after sharing a photo of her cabinet members at the Black History Museum and Cultural Center of Virginia in Richmond. The photo, taken during a session marking the largest appointment of Black cabinet officials in Virginia's history, was shared on X with a caption praising the 'most diverse cabinet Virginia has ever seen.' Conservative critics quickly seized on the image, arguing it contained 'too many Black people' to be considered diverse. Several MAGA influencers and conservative figures, including Katie Miller, Geiger Capital, and Jack Posobiec, posted on social media claiming the cabinet's composition was not diverse but rather 'anti-White.' They incorrectly counted the people in the photo rather than the full cabinet, which includes two non-Black members. item.title: Fox News accidentally interviews Trump rally opponent who compares supporters to Jonestown cult
item.description: Fox News faced backlash after accidentally interviewing a Trump opponent at a Senate rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina. The man, identified as 'Tom,' made a controversial comparison to the Jonestown Massacre, stating, 'Well, in the late 70s, I was a little too young to go to South America for the Jonestown Massacre. But this is as close as I'll ever get, so that's why I'm here. There's nothing like seeing a cult right up front.' Ryan Fournier, founder of Students for Trump, called the incident 'UNREAL' and demanded security find the man immediately. item.title: Kate Jackson's Iconic Role in Charlie's Angels and Her Signature Style in the 1970s
item.description: Lucy Kate Jackson, born October 29, 1948, is an American actress and television producer who rose to international fame in the mid-1970s as the intelligent and level-headed leader of the original Charlie's Angels. Her career took a significant turn in 1976 when she helped develop and star in ABC's hit series Charlie's Angels, portraying Sabrina Duncan, the smart, grounded, and intuitive leader of the trio alongside Farrah Fawcett and Jaclyn Smith. Jackson played a key role in pitching the show's concept, reportedly suggesting the name 'Charlie's Angels' after seeing a picture of angels in a producer's office. Unlike her co-stars' glamorous and bombshell aesthetics, Jackson stood out for her effortless, tailored sophistication, featuring a signature short brunette shag haircut with soft bangs that became widely copied in the mid-to-late 1970s. item.title: Inflation concerns escalate ahead of midterm elections as PCE index hits 3.6%
item.description: The latest inflation report has intensified economic concerns for President Donald Trump and the Republican Party just days before the midterm elections. According to the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, which is the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, prices rose at an annual rate of 3.6% in September, marking the highest level since May. This development has sparked warnings from economists and political figures alike. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, highlighted the worsening inflation trend on social media, stating that "Inflation is back near a 3-year high" and attributing much of the increase to ongoing conflicts in Iran. Representative Ted Lieu (D-CA) quickly seized on the data, criticizing Trump's economic policies as "sucking" and declaring that "The Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation (PCE) rose again, this time to 3.6%, the highest since May." item.title: Thailand's Pongsapak Laopakdee opens with 63 to lead Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship
item.description: The opening round of the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship at Te Arai Links' South Course in New Zealand saw Thailand's Pongsapak 'Fifa' Laopakdee take the lead with an eight-under 63, despite challenging wind conditions exceeding 30 mph. The defending champion, who overcame a six-stroke deficit to win in Dubai last year, now aims to become only the second player to win consecutive Asia-Pacific Amateur titles, following Hideki Matsuyama's 2010-2011 victories. Laopakdee's round featured a chip-in eagle on the ninth and nearly holed out on the 15th, showcasing his skill under difficult conditions. Australia's Harry Takis, ranked No. 21 in the World Amateur Golf Ranking, carded a 70 with an eagle on the seventh, leading the field as the highest-ranked player. New Zealand's Joshua Bai, a University of Florida golfer, opened with a five-under 66, three shots behind Laopakdee, and has a strong history in the championship, having won the North & South Amateur earlier this year. item.title: Akwa Ibom Health Workers and CSOs Highlight Systemic Barriers to HIV, TB, and Malaria Services
item.description: Civil society organizations and health workers in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, have identified significant barriers preventing vulnerable populations from accessing essential healthcare services for HIV, tuberculosis (TB), and malaria. Despite existing government policies, stigma, cultural restrictions, inadequate health facilities, and confidentiality concerns continue to hinder service uptake. During a one-day meeting in Uyo, stakeholders emphasized the need for urgent government action to improve accessibility for women and other marginalized groups. Key recommendations included enhancing public awareness of available services, training health workers to provide non-discriminatory care, and equipping primary healthcare centers to better serve communities. Participants also stressed the importance of consistent data collection to track disease cases and assess policy implementation. item.title: Patrick Stewart, Iconic 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' Actor, Passes Away at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the renowned actor celebrated for his iconic roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' and Professor Charles Xavier in the 'X-Men' film series, has died at the age of 86. According to a statement from his longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, Stewart passed away at his Los Angeles home following a brief but poignant battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. The statement described his final moments as filled with family, friends, live music, prayer, tears, and laughter, reflecting the profound impact he had on those around him throughout his career. Stewart's career began in British theater, with decades of classical work before he gained international fame in the late 1980s. His casting as Captain Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' was initially met with skepticism from Star Trek creator Gene Roddenberry, who doubted a 'bald Brit' could lead the series. item.title: Justice Department opposes consolidation of Epstein survivor lawsuits in federal court
item.description: The Justice Department under President Donald Trump is opposing efforts to consolidate two lawsuits filed by Jeffrey Epstein survivors who claim the FBI failed to act on their reports. The push for consolidation began with U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon, a Trump appointee, who initially ruled that Maria Farmer's case, filed in Washington in May 2025, should be transferred to Florida where it would be handled by Judge David Leibowitz, a Biden appointee overseeing the Jane Doe 1 et al. v. United States case. Farmer, one of the earliest known Epstein victims, alleged in her lawsuit that she reported Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to the FBI in 1996, but the agency took no action in violation of its policies. The Doe case, brought by Laura Newman, Sandra Ward, and 32 Jane Does, has been ongoing since 2024 and involves claims against the FBI. item.title: Trump's Antisemitism Task Force Leader Threatened to Choke Jewish Intern, Harvard Report Reveals
item.description: A Harvard Crimson investigation has uncovered alarming allegations against Leo Terrell, who leads President Donald Trump’s antisemitism task force. According to the report, Terrell threatened to choke a Jewish intern with a computer charger, isolated Jewish interns, berated them, and repeatedly threatened their jobs or careers. item.description: A recent study conducted by researchers at Tongji University in China has revealed that breaking resistance training into short, frequent sessions throughout the day can produce strength and endurance gains similar to those achieved through a single, continuous workout. Both groups used a Smith machine under expert supervision, with weights progressively increased over time. item.description: A groundbreaking study published in Communications Biology has uncovered how reinforcement learning shapes both the selection of motor actions and the timing of their execution in the Aplysia feeding circuit. Their findings reveal that reinforcement biases motor program selection toward ingestive behaviors while simultaneously shortening the duration of these actions by advancing the transition from protraction to retraction phases in feeding movements. These include recognizing the spiral early, challenging the validity of catastrophic thoughts, grounding oneself in the present moment, and developing a structured plan for potential outcomes. item.description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on October 6 that Belgian-American physicist and astrophysicist Francis Halzen has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This marks the first unshared Physics Nobel since 1992 and the fifth in history related to neutrinos. Halzen's work bridges particle physics and astrophysics, focusing on the detection of neutrinos, often called 'ghost particles' due to their near-invisibility and ability to pass through matter without interaction. The article details the historical context of neutrino research, from Wolfgang Pauli's 1931 theoretical prediction to the 1956 experimental confirmation by Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines. item.title: Daily Fiber Supplement Shows Promise in Reducing Knee Arthritis Pain and Enhancing Muscle Strength
item.description: A clinical trial led by researchers at the University of Nottingham has revealed that a daily prebiotic fiber supplement, specifically inulin, can significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis (OA) pain while improving muscle strength. The study, published in the journal Nutrients, involved 117 adults with knee OA who were assigned to one of four treatment groups: inulin alone, digital physical therapy exercises (PSE) alone, a combination of inulin and PSE, or a placebo. Participants taking inulin experienced notable pain reduction, improved grip strength, and decreased pain sensitivity compared to those in the physical therapy group. The supplement also demonstrated a much higher adherence rate, with only 3.6% dropout in the inulin group versus 21% in the physical therapy group. Inulin, a naturally occurring fiber found in foods like chicory root and Jerusalem artichokes, is not broken down by digestive enzymes but instead nourishes beneficial gut bacteria in the large intestine. item.title: Critical UEFI Firmware Flaw Affects Most Servers, Allows Pre-Boot Code Execution
item.description: A critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, has been discovered in the TianoCore EDK II open-source codebase used by most server vendors and data centers for UEFI firmware. The flaw, rated 9.5 out of 10 in severity, is a memory-corruption issue in the ICMP component that allows attackers to execute malicious code before the operating system and firmware defenses like Secure Boot activate. The vulnerability affects the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which handles network boot processes, enabling attackers to send malicious ICMP error messages that overwrite memory buffers. This can lead to code execution in ring 0, the most privileged CPU level, before security mechanisms like TPM and Secure Boot are engaged. The flaw has been present for 16 years and impacts systems that boot from network resources, including servers, storage equipment, and devices relying on EDK2-based firmware. item.title: Ukrainian Authorities Face Growing Scrutiny Over Forced Mobilization Practices
item.description: In Ukrainian cities, the routine checks of military registration documents and the forcible transfer of men to Territorial Recruitment Centers (TCCs) have become a common feature of wartime life. TCC personnel and police officers conduct vehicle stops, pedestrian inspections, and joint raids, often using physical force. Mobile teams frequently change locations, with residents warning each other through local Telegram groups. Social media and news outlets have documented cases of beatings, unlawful detentions, and denial of access to lawyers. The Ukrainian ombudsman has reported a significant increase in complaints about these practices, with some cases leading to criminal convictions. item.description: A recent incident involving a medical examination has sparked discussion about patient-doctor communication and the importance of clear, respectful dialogue in healthcare settings. The patient, who wishes to remain anonymous, described an encounter with a physician who, during a routine gynecological exam, made comments that were both unexpected and unsettling. The doctor reportedly looked at the patient's genital area and then stated three words that the patient found shocking. While the exact words were not disclosed, the patient expressed concern about the appropriateness of the remarks and the lack of explanation provided. This incident highlights the need for healthcare providers to maintain professionalism and ensure that patients feel comfortable and informed during examinations. Medical ethics require that doctors communicate clearly with patients, explaining procedures and any observations made during exams. item.title: NME releases 2025-2026 coffee table book featuring 50 emerging artists with exclusive content
item.description: NME has launched 'NME The Cover 2025-2026', a 300-page hardcover coffee table book collecting 50 stories from its weekly franchise that champions emerging artists globally. The third edition in the annually released series features artists such as Maruja, Balu Brigada, Die Spitz, Gigi Perez, BOYNEXTDOOR, and many others, with bespoke artwork, interviews, and previously unseen photography. The book is available for purchase with a 20% launch discount, with orders beginning dispatch on November 6. Free UK delivery is offered, and international shipping is free on orders over £200. The Cover relaunched in May 2023 with the goal of connecting emerging artists with NME's audience of millions of music fans. item.title: Sauna Bathing Temporarily Boosts Immune Cell Circulation, Study Finds
item.description: A recent study conducted by researchers in Finland has revealed that a single 30-minute sauna session, followed by a brief cold shower, triggers a temporary surge in white blood cells circulating in the bloodstream. The findings, published in the journal Temperature, indicate that sauna bathing mobilizes immune cells that typically reside in tissues, allowing them to move more freely throughout the body. This increased circulation enhances the body's ability to monitor for pathogens such as bacteria and viruses. The study measured various types of white blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, which are critical for immune responses. Neutrophils act as first responders to infections, while lymphocytes are involved in recognizing specific threats and producing antibodies. The increase in these cells was observed immediately after the sauna session but returned to baseline levels within 30 minutes. item.title: Faith Domergue: A 1950s Horror and Sci-Fi Star Known for Her Dark Beauty
item.description: Faith Domergue (1924 or 1925–1999) was an American actress celebrated for her dark beauty and significant roles in 1950s science fiction and horror films. Discovered as a teenager by Howard Hughes, she was signed to a contract and groomed for stardom, though her early career faced delays and limited opportunities. Domergue gained lasting recognition in the mid-1950s with appearances in cult classics such as This Island Earth (1955), It Came from Beneath the Sea (1955), and Cult of the Cobra (1955), earning her a place among the era’s early 'scream queens.' Her striking features and intense screen presence made her a distinctive figure in mid-century genre cinema. These films, now considered classics, highlight her ability to captivate audiences with her dramatic presence. Domergue's work in these movies cemented her legacy as a memorable face of 1950s science fiction and film noir. item.title: Samsung TV's Pet Care feature raises privacy concerns over data sharing with advertisers
item.description: In April 2025, Samsung introduced Vision AI sets with features called Pet Care and Family Care, which could detect dog barks or baby cries in an empty room and send alerts to owners' phones. The company stated these features only worked when the TV was turned off. However, on October 23, 2026, a reverse engineer known as log4j shared findings suggesting Samsung TVs send data about barks, cries, sensor readings, and camera streaming duration to Samsung servers. The researcher discovered this through unpatched security flaws that allowed full control of the TV, revealing sound-classification models, screen capture logs, and cross-device advertising IDs. Samsung's automatic content recognition (ACR) system, which samples screen content twice per second, has been documented for years, but the new claims involve potential audio data collection. The researcher alleges that even when ACR is turned off, data might still be transmitted. Samsung has disputed the claims, stating that viewing-reco

item.title: GOP Strategist Criticizes Ex-Trump Aide's Proposal to Cut Ukraine Funding to End War
item.description: On Wednesday's episode of CNN's 'NewsNight,' guest-hosted by Michael Smerconish, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton engaged in a heated exchange with Caroline Sunshine, a former Trump White House aide, over her proposal to end the Ukraine-Russia conflict by cutting U.S. funding to Ukraine. Sunshine argued that the U.S. should withdraw financial support to force Ukraine to negotiate a peace deal, stating that Ukraine is not a NATO ally and the U.S. has no role in the war except to end it. Singleton strongly opposed the idea, calling it 'the most absurd thing' and accusing Sunshine of being 'incredibly naive.' He emphasized that Russia, not Ukraine, initiated the conflict, noting that 'it wasn't the Ukrainians. It was the Russians.' Singleton further criticized Sunshine for suggesting that Ukraine should be pressured to negotiate, arguing that the U.S. has never taken such a stance before. item.title: Vali Myers: Australian Artist and Spiritual Pioneer of Positano
item.description: Vali Myers, widely known as the 'Witch of Positano,' was an Australian artist, dancer, and mystic whose life spanned the post-war avant-garde scenes of Paris, New York's Chelsea Hotel, and a remote Italian canyon. Born in Sydney in 1930, Myers became a prominent figure in the Beatnik movement in Paris, where she was photographed by Ed van der Elsken for his book 'Love on the Left Bank.' She associated with cultural icons like Jean Cocteau, Allen Ginsberg, and Jean-Paul Sartre. After overcoming an opium addiction, Myers retreated with her partner Rudi Rappold to a cliffside ravine near Positano, Italy, where they lived in an abandoned stone structure without modern amenities. For decades, she immersed herself in nature, creating intricate pen-and-ink and watercolor drawings that depicted mystical themes, animal forms, and powerful representations of femininity. She also established a wildlife sanctuary for rescued animals, contributing to the area's protection as a WWF oasis. Myers main

item.title: Bluesky Blocks Links to DHS Employee Data Leak, Citing Safety Concerns
item.description: Bluesky has blocked links to a newly leaked archive containing records of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees and contractors, labeling the pages as 'malicious.' The files include personal contact information such as email addresses and phone numbers, shared without authorization, which violates Bluesky's community guidelines. The company chose to block the links rather than remove individual posts to avoid restricting public discussion or broader access to reporting on the leak. The DHS records, published by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), detail employee names, contact information, and internal group memberships, including those tied to surveillance and undercover operations. A WIRED investigation revealed the files provide insight into DHS organizational structure, from leadership to individual immigration agents, and who has access to certain technologies. item.title: Snow Peak Campfield: A Japanese-Inspired Retreat on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula
item.description: Snow Peak Campfield, located on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula, offers a unique blend of Japanese design and Pacific Northwest natural beauty. The campfield features Jyubako suites, small cabins made of pale pine and plywood, each approximately 200 square feet with a queen bed, futon, kitchenette, and private bathroom. Priced from $130 per night, these cabins are designed to encourage guests to stay connected with nature, with low furniture that positions the eye at the top edge of the glass door to the porch, gently nudging guests outside. The main attraction is the Ofuro, a Japanese-style bathhouse with a hot pool maintained at 104 degrees, a hinoki cypress sauna, cold plunge, and showers. The bathhouse is thoughtfully designed with angled beams echoing the surrounding trees and an open side facing a grove of alders at the edge of a pond. The Long Beach Peninsula, where the campfield is situated, is known for its wide sandy beaches, razor clamming, kite flying, and storm watching.

item.title: MUHC Researchers Identify New Vesicles Linked to Cancer Cell Migration and Metastasis
item.description: Researchers at McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) have identified a novel mechanism by which migrating cancer cells communicate and spread throughout the body. The study, led by Prof. Julia Burnier and PhD student Thupten Tsering, reveals that cancer cells release specialized structures called motile vesicles (MoVes), which carry genetic material including cancer-associated mutations. These vesicles, previously thought to be cellular waste, are now understood to play a critical role in cell-to-cell communication during cancer progression. The discovery emerged unexpectedly while investigating how cancer cells release DNA, leading to the identification of MoVes as a key component in the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process. EMT is a biological mechanism that allows cells to become more mobile and invasive, contributing to tumor progression and treatment resistance. item.title: Early Voting by Black Voters Rises in Southern States Ahead of 2026 Midterms
item.description:
Early voting among Black Americans has increased significantly ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, particularly in Southern states where Republican redistricting efforts have targeted majority-Black congressional districts. According to The Bulwark, Black voters have cast more than 160,000 additional ballots compared with the same stage of the 2022 midterm elections, raising questions about whether Republican efforts to reshape electoral districts could have unintended political consequences.
The developments follow the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, a case that originated in Louisiana and weakened the protections provided by Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Following the decision, Republicans in several states moved to redraw congressional maps and dismantle majority-Black districts. item.title: Trump Administration Challenges Court Order on Park Closure for Golf Course Renovation
item.description: The Trump administration's Justice Department has raised objections to a federal court order requiring detailed notice before closing East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C., for a golf course renovation. In a filing with the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, the department argued that the court's requirements for 'prompt notice' and extensive documentation, including naming every individual involved and assessing the impact on the park, are overly burdensome. The closure, scheduled for November 15, is part of a plan to replace the current public golf course with a 'World Class, championship-level golf course' designed by Tom Fazio, capable of hosting major tournaments like the U.S. Open and the Ryder Cup. The National Park Service has signed a new lease with National Links Trust, the company currently operating the East Potomac Golf Course, which will cease operations by the closure date but will continue managing Rock Creek and Langston golf courses. item.description: Dancing With the Stars season 35 celebrated Halloween with a horror movie-themed episode, featuring performances inspired by films such as Saw, Black Swan, and Joker. The episode marked the first perfect score of the season when Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson earned a 40/40 for their contemporary dance to 'Toxic' by 2WEI, inspired by the horror film Saw. item.description: After months of hesitation and internal debate, European leaders are signaling a decisive shift toward direct engagement with Russia to address the Ukraine conflict and reshape continental security architecture. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre recently held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, marking a significant step in Europe's diplomatic approach. While lacking formal mandates, their initiative positioned Nordic leaders as key interlocutors, with the Kremlin confirming plans for continued direct communication. The European Commission and Council are preparing a joint delegation, led by Bjoern Seibert, to join upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi, aiming for a multilateral format involving Europeans, Ukrainians, Americans, and Russians—a departure from previous US-centric negotiations. item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's chief planner, from his position on the Joint Chiefs of Staff without providing an explanation, according to The Atlantic. Sylvia, who led the Joint Staff's strategy, plans and policy directorate (J5), is the second person to be removed from that role within a year, following the forced retirement of his predecessor, Army Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee. item.description: The news article details multiple instances of measles transmission from South Carolina to Washington state within a two-week period. These four individuals then visited schools, healthcare facilities, and a church, causing nine additional cases among their contacts and one person exposed in a public location, totaling 14 cases from January 15 to February 17. item.description: According to a New York Times report, President Donald Trump's behavior has become increasingly erratic behind closed doors, causing concern among those closest to him. The report, based on interviews with 16 current and former administration officials and Trump allies, reveals a sense of gloom descending on the White House less than a week before Election Day. Trump has been shrinking his circle of confidants, lashing out at critics, and dismissing polls showing his unpopularity. item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Declines to Investigate Starlink Service Disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: A bipartisan group of nine U.S. senators, comprising four Republicans and five Democrats, has been denied a request to investigate the throttling of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine. The Defense Department's inspector general (IG) declined the lawmakers' inquiry, stating that the Air Force is better equipped to address concerns regarding the slowdown. The senators sought the probe after Ukrainian officials reported that connection speeds on both Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, had been reduced, hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones. A congressional aide, speaking anonymously, characterized the IG's decision as a refusal to examine Musk and Starlink's role, despite the office's capability to do so. item.title: 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu Captured in Vibrant Kodachrome Photos
item.description: The 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu, Hawaii, is vividly captured through a series of vintage Kodachrome photographs, offering a nostalgic glimpse into mid-century Hawaiian culture and traditions. Established in 1946 to celebrate Hawaiian heritage, Aloha Week featured a vibrant array of cultural elements including colorful floral floats, pāʻū riders in traditional attire, marching bands, and the Royal Court parading through Waikiki's streets. The Kodachrome film's rich, saturated colors beautifully preserved the tropical flowers, bright costumes, and festive atmosphere of the event, providing a detailed visual record of the parade's pageantry. Among the images are specific scenes such as a Chinese-themed float with members of a Lion Dance organization, the Bridge of Friendship, Civic Club displays, debutantes from Kaimuki JCC, and the King and Queen of Aloha Week, Henry Rosa and Barbara Kukaua. item.title: Stripe Billing Coordination Design Prevents Duplicate Payment Attempts
item.description: Stripe Billing has a built-in feature called Smart Retries that automatically handles failed subscription payments by retrying at optimal times based on network and issuer signals. However, when merchants add a recovery layer on top of Stripe's system, a coordination problem arises: two systems may attempt to retry the same failed payment, leading to duplicated attempts, wasted resources, and potential double-charging. The Swipe Again team, which provides a recovery solution for Stripe Billing merchants, has developed a coordination design that integrates with Stripe's native retry system rather than competing with it. Their approach reads Stripe's current state before each retry decision, using observable invoice data such as attempt_count, next_payment_attempt, and decline codes. The system defers attempts if Stripe is about to retry within 24 hours, fires into gaps in Stripe's schedule, and only runs full recovery plans when Stripe has exhausted its retry attempts. item.description: Michael Gleason, husband of Amy Gleason, who served as acting administrator of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), began working as a senior adviser in the Health and Human Services Department's Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation in May 2025. His appointment came just 33 days after significant layoffs at the Health and Human Services Department (HHS), which had been heavily impacted by DOGE-driven cuts. This connection is particularly notable given that Graham, who succeeded her late brother Lindsey Graham—a prominent supporter of Ukraine—faces a critical Senate race against Democrat Annie Andrews next week. item.title: MAGA Podcast Hosts Clash with Analyst Over Trump Administration's Policies
item.description: The pro-MAGA podcast 'The Charlie Kirk Show' descended into chaos during a segment where former Republican strategist Tim Miller challenged the hosts' claims about President Donald Trump's record. The exchange, which occurred less than a week before the midterm elections, covered immigration enforcement, military actions in Iran, and economic policies. Miller began by expressing horror over the shooting of the show's founder, Charlie Kirk, at a Utah Valley University event last year, condemning conspiracy theories surrounding the incident. He then criticized Trump for betraying his base, citing the Iran war as a costly military decision that has increased interest rates, gas prices, and food costs for Americans. Miller also addressed the killing of two U.S. citizens by federal agents in Minneapolis, which the hosts dismissed as media bias. item.description:
President Donald Trump has taken to his Truth Social platform to express frustration over the Alaska ballot, where Republicans are concerned about GOP Senator Dan Sullivan facing a minor candidate with the same name. Trump's Justice Department is suing Alaska to prevent certification of a ballot featuring both Dan Sullivans, alleging election fraud. Trump accused Democratic candidate Mary Peltola and her associates of orchestrating a scheme to place a candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, claiming it constitutes election fraud and perjury. item.title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General over alleged deceptive pricing practices
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 20 states have filed a lawsuit against Dollar General, alleging deceptive pricing practices that have overcharged consumers for years. The complaint states that Dollar General repeatedly mislabeled prices, failed to correct discrepancies despite knowing about the issue, and extracted millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges from vulnerable shoppers. The FTC and states claim that thousands of stores have taken advantage of consumers, with tens of thousands of complaints filed nationwide about advertised prices not being honored. Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection, stated that Dollar General has 'betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last.' item.title: Federal Government Sues Idaho Over Water Rights for Nuclear Laboratory
item.description: The U.S. federal government has filed a lawsuit against the state of Idaho, seeking to block the state from curtailing water use at Idaho National Laboratory and from administering federal water rights. The lawsuit, filed on September 11 in U.S. District Court, argues that the federal government has supremacy over state regulations under the Constitution's supremacy clause. Idaho's water curtailment order, issued by Director Mathew Weaver of the Idaho Department of Water Resources, would have restricted water use for the laboratory, which holds a water right of 35,000 acre-feet annually. The federal government claims that the state's actions violate constitutional principles by attempting to directly regulate federal agencies without congressional authorization. Idaho's response, submitted on October 16, denies the allegations and countersues, asserting that the federal government must follow the same water laws as all other users in Idaho. item.title: FDA scientists oppose Health Secretary Kennedy's push to allow unapproved peptide drugs
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has encountered significant resistance from Food and Drug Administration (FDA) scientists regarding his efforts to expand access to injectable peptide drugs. According to an Associated Press report, six sources familiar with the policy development revealed that most FDA scientific staff opposed the initiative, expressing concerns that it could undermine the agency's mission to prevent unproven health products from entering the U.S. market. Kennedy's Department of Health and Human Services initially sought a regulation that would classify certain peptides as safe for use by compounding pharmacies, which create customized medications. However, FDA officials warned that scientific staff had substantial safety concerns and would not endorse a regulation declaring these substances safe. item.title: LaKeith Stanfield and Ben Wheatley Replace Rob Savage in 'Molepeople' Horror Film
item.description: Paramount Primal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster have announced significant changes to their upcoming horror film 'Molepeople.' LaKeith Stanfield, who was previously announced as a star, has exited the project, and director Rob Savage has departed due to scheduling conflicts. Ben Wheatley, known for his work on films like 'Normal' and 'Kill List,' will now take over as director. The film, which was unveiled during Blumhouse Atomic Monster's New York Comic-Con presentation earlier this month, follows a man who descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City and discovers a 'twisted society' living there. Written by Nathan Elston, 'Molepeople' is co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal, with Paramount handling worldwide distribution. The film is scheduled for a theatrical release on August 27, 2027. Producers include Jason Blum, J.D. Lifshitz, Raphael Margules, and James Harris. item.title: Trump demands removal of Democratic candidate from Alaska Senate race, accuses Democrats of election fraud
item.description: President Donald Trump has issued a series of aggressive statements on his Truth Social platform, accusing Democratic officials in Alaska of election fraud and demanding the removal of Senate candidate Mary Peltola from the ballot. Trump's claims stem from a New York Times investigation that linked Peltola's campaign and national Democratic operatives to efforts to recruit a candidate named Dan Sullivan for the Alaska Senate race. Trump alleged that Democrats 'illegally searched for, and recruited' Dan Sullivan to run against Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, claiming this was an attempt to 'defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election.' He further accused Peltola's campaign of making 'false statements under oath in Federal Court,' which he labeled as perjury, and demanded that she face 'very serious consequences.' item.title: Ramaswamy's attack ad backfires in Ohio governor race, GOP fears internal fallout
item.description: According to an internal GOP poll obtained by Axios, Republicans are concerned that Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad is harming his bid for governor of Ohio. The survey, commissioned by a Republican group, shows Democrat Amy Acton leading by eight points, up from a two-point lead she had before the ad began circulating on October 19. The poll, conducted among 800 likely voters from October 23 to 26, found Acton's support rising from 47 percent to 50 percent, while Ramaswamy's support dropped from 45 percent to 42 percent. Eighty-six percent of respondents were aware of the ad, and those who knew about it were twice as likely to favor Acton, according to a memo. A separate Suffolk University poll also indicated a four-point gap, narrower than the nine-point lead shown in late September. The ad features Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing her daughter of lying about her childhood. item.description: During a segment on the Ohio governor's race, MS NOW host Alicia Menendez intervened to correct a guest who referred to President Donald Trump as a 'convicted sex offender.' The discussion initially focused on Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown criticizing a campaign ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother, who lost custody after refusing to protect her from sexual assault by her stepfather. Brown expressed hope that Republican Senator Jon Husted would pressure Vivek Ramaswamy to withdraw the ad, but noted Husted instead aligned with Governor Mike DeWine, Trump, and JD Vance in defending it. Guest Richard Stengel then claimed Trump 'gets a pass' for conduct that would disqualify other politicians, stating he was a 'convicted sex offender' and suffering from 'frontal lobe dementia' without providing evidence. item.title: Nanotyrannus Skeleton Fetches $47.3 Million at New York Auction, Sparking Scientific Debate
item.description: The mounted skeleton of a newly identified dinosaur, nicknamed Jodi, has sold at auction for $47.3 million, making it the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold. The 10-foot-tall skeleton, initially mistaken for a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex, was confirmed by researchers to belong to a distinct genus, Nanotyrannus, in October 2023. The auction, conducted by Sotheby's in New York, saw intense bidding among six parties over a 12-minute period. The sale has reignited discussions within the scientific community about the ethics of private fossil sales versus public display. Sotheby's described Jodi as an 'excellent exhibition-ready' skeleton with 191 fossil elements and a nearly complete skull, noting it is one of only three such skeletons known to science. The skeleton was discovered in Montana's Hell Creek Formation by rancher Jodi Pierson and later excavated by commercial paleontologist Clayton Phipps, who also discovered the famous 'Dueling Dinosaurs' fossil. item.title: Trump faces potential new Espionage Act charges as DOJ strategy in Comey case could impact future cases
item.description: The Justice Department is laying the groundwork for potential new Espionage Act charges against former President Donald Trump by filing a criminal information in a case against former FBI Director James Comey, according to legal experts. The filing, made on October 5, 2026, just before the 10-year deadline for Espionage Act prosecutions expired, aims to establish a legal precedent that could help prosecutors bypass the need for a grand jury in future cases involving Trump. The case against Comey, which prosecutors argue meets the 10-year deadline set by Congress, has drawn attention because it could set a precedent for how the Justice Department handles charges related to Trump's alleged mishandling of classified documents at Mar-a-Lago. Comey's lawyers have challenged the filing, arguing that it allows the government to keep allegations 'hanging over' a defendant indefinitely without a grand jury indictment. item.title: Julia Roberts' Early Breakthrough Role in 'Mystic Pizza' (1988) Revealed
item.description: The filming of Mystic Pizza in the fall of 1987 marked a pivotal moment in Julia Roberts' career, propelling her to fame just two years before she became a global superstar. At 19, Roberts was relatively unknown, having been cast as the fiery, rebellious Daisy Araújo despite not being the first choice. Director Donald Petrie chose her for her infectious laugh and raw talent, which allowed her to hold her own alongside more seasoned actors. Roberts described Daisy as 'full of fire and full of spice,' and the role provided her with a creative 'free-for-all' that let her act without restraint. Her co-stars later recalled that Roberts was the most fun on set, thanks to her energetic and happy nature. The movie, set in Mystic, Connecticut, was filmed in a replica set built in a warehouse and a converted home in Stonington, as the real Mystic Pizza was too small for filming. item.title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump Administration's Use of Taxpayer Funds for Campaign Ads
item.description: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan has issued a ruling blocking the Trump administration from using $20 million in taxpayer funds for television advertisements promoting President Trump. The judge criticized the administration's unfulfilled promise to stop using public money for the ads, noting that the advertisements continued to air with the 'Paid for by the U.S. Government' disclosure for at least another week after Trump's October 5 pledge. The ruling follows a separate court order in New York that had already blocked the taxpayer-funded advertisements through mid-November, well beyond the November 3, 2026, elections. Judge AliKhan concluded that officials likely used public dollars to unlawfully finance a national campaign in the final weeks before the November 2026 elections. item.title: Border Security Official Uses Former Secretary's Luxury Jet Amid Feud
item.description: Border Security Official Tom Homan, a vocal critic of former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, has reportedly been using a luxury Gulfstream jet that was previously associated with Noem, according to a Substack newsletter called The PunchUp. The jet, a $53 million Gulfstream G650 with tail number N472US, flew from Washington's Reagan National Airport to San Juan, Puerto Rico, last Tuesday and then to West Palm Beach the following day. This usage comes amid a bitter feud between Homan and Noem, who was fired as Homeland Security Secretary in March 2026 following a series of controversies, including her use of a $200 million Gulfstream G700 fleet and a leased Boeing 737 with luxury amenities. The feud intensified after two American citizens were killed during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis, leading to Trump appointing Homan to oversee the operation as a rebuke to Noem. item.title: FDA streamlines gene therapy approvals, Missouri AG targets Lilly's 340B data demands
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published draft guidance aimed at streamlining approvals for individualized gene therapies, a move welcomed by rare disease advocates who have long criticized the agency's previous approach. Under the current system, companies must submit separate drug approval applications for each patient's customized gene therapy, even when using fundamentally the same method to target different genes. This process has been deemed prohibitively expensive by advocates, who argue it creates unnecessary regulatory burdens. The new draft guidance formalizes a 'plausible mechanism pathway,' offering clearer rules for licensing and updating gene editing treatments. Separately, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Eli Lilly, demanding the company stop requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program. item.title: Saab introduces Sea Giraffe AMB D radar with 155-mile air detection range and anti-jamming capabilities
item.description: Saab, the Swedish defense company, has unveiled its latest naval radar system, the Sea Giraffe AMB D, designed to detect and track air and surface threats at extended ranges. The radar boasts a 155-mile (250-kilometer) detection range for air targets and 31 miles (50 kilometers) for surface targets. Built on the Sea Giraffe AMB family, the new system integrates active electronically scanned array (AESA) technology with a software-defined architecture, enabling rapid beam steering and multi-tasking capabilities. This allows the radar to monitor multiple areas simultaneously while providing timely threat information. The system incorporates electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) to resist jamming attempts by adversaries, a critical feature in modern electronic warfare environments. Saab emphasizes the radar's modular design, which supports integration with other naval systems and allows for continuous software upgrades without requiring hardware replacement. item.title: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom says Trump's rally visit shows GOP anxiety as race tightens
item.description: Mississippi Democratic Senate nominee Scott Colom has responded to President Donald Trump's recent rally in his state, calling it a sign of Republican anxiety and using the event to bolster his fundraising efforts. In a fundraising email sent Wednesday, Colom detailed how Trump's Monday rally at Crossroads Arena in Corinth targeted him and his campaign, accusing the former president of spreading 'hate and lies' about him. Trump attended the event to support Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.), whom Colom is challenging in a Senate race that has become unexpectedly competitive in a traditionally Republican state. Colom stated, 'I think we're under their skin,' suggesting that the Republican Party's heightened focus on his campaign indicates they are feeling threatened. item.title: Susan Saint James: Early Career and Iconic 1960s Television Roles
item.description: Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James passed away on October 26, 2026, at the age of 80 after battling pancreatic cancer. While she gained widespread recognition in the 1970s and 1980s through roles in 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie,' her career began to take shape in the mid-to-late 1960s. At age 20, she landed her first major television role in the pilot film 'Fame Is the Name of the Game,' portraying Peggy Maxwell, a sharp editorial research assistant. The pilot was developed into a full series called 'The Name of the Game' in 1968, where she continued her role. Her performance earned her three Emmy nominations and a win for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series in 1969. Saint James distinguished herself in an era of traditional Hollywood glamour by embracing a relatable 'girl next door' persona rather than high-fashion modeling looks. item.title: Disney Bus Driver Shares Journey from Church Minister to Theme Park Employment at 51
item.description: Michael Bowen, a 51-year-old bus driver at Walt Disney World, shares his career transition from a church minister to working at Disney. After years in religious ministry, Bowen felt unfulfilled and sought a change. In 2017, during a vacation to Florida, he realized he could pursue a career as a Disney bus driver. He moved to Florida in 2020 at age 44, after obtaining a Florida driver's license, and began working as a bus driver for Disney. He appreciated the stable job with benefits like health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plans, which were unavailable in his previous church positions. In 2022, Bowen left Disney following a difficult divorce, moving to Oregon where he drove city buses but remained unhappy. He later met his current wife through his Disney-focused YouTube channel, 'Incognito Mouse,' and returned to Disney in 2026 at age 50. item.title: Right-Wing Activist James O'Keefe Charged with Unlawful Voting in Minnesota Polling Place Stunt
item.description: Conservative provocateur James O'Keefe, founder of O'Keefe Media Group, has been criminally charged with identity theft and unlawful voting following a polling place stunt in Minneapolis during Minnesota's primary election. The incident, which was captured in videos posted online in August, involved members of O'Keefe's group, dubbed the 'Justice League,' attempting to test Minnesota's voter vouching system. During the stunt, one group member dressed in a burqa and another used an accent while posing as a voter named 'William Pomeranz,' a real Minneapolis registered voter. The group claimed they were merely asking election workers about the vouching process, not impersonating anyone. However, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced criminal charges against O'Keefe and Cam Higby, alleging identity theft and unlawful voting. item.description: The article examines recent MAGA rallies held in October 2026, noting that speakers at these events rarely mentioned Donald Trump, a stark contrast to previous years. The author, an anthropologist who has studied Trump and the MAGA movement for years, attended rallies in Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Mississippi, observing a noticeable decline in crowd enthusiasm compared to 2024 events. item.description: The article criticizes former President Donald Trump for publicly disclosing that the U.S. is delaying a major military offensive against Iran until after the upcoming election. The author argues that Trump's admission, made during a press briefing, unnecessarily reveals the political vulnerability of the military operation to Iran, potentially giving the Iranian government time to prepare countermeasures. The piece emphasizes that Trump's decision to share this information with the media, rather than providing a more strategic explanation, puts U.S. troops at greater risk by making the military's position transparent to adversaries. The article notes that Trump's statement contradicts the usual practice of keeping military strategies confidential, especially when they involve potential conflicts with foreign powers. item.description:
Joe Rogan, the popular podcaster known for his significant influence on political discourse, has shifted from his previous endorsement of Donald Trump to expressing growing criticism of the president's policies, particularly regarding foreign affairs and domestic governance. 'What Trump stood for, some of it turned out to not be real,' Rogan stated during a recent conversation with actor Michael Douglas, adding that the president's promise of 'no wars' was contradicted by the current military engagement with Iran, which he described as 'a giant quagmire.'

item.description: Mary Trump, the niece of former President Donald Trump, has issued a stark warning about her uncle's alleged plan to manipulate the upcoming midterm elections. item.description: Vice President JD Vance has become the center of a Brazilian police investigation regarding whether his co-founded donor network, the Rockbridge Network, illegally supported Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign. Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the investigation following Bolsonaro's loss in the October 25 runoff election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. item.description: CBS's '60 Minutes' has experienced a significant ratings decline in its latest episode, drawing only 5.64 million total viewers and 558,000 viewers in the 25-54 demographic, according to Nielsen figures obtained by Status' Oliver Darcy. This performance marks a notable drop from historical averages, as the sixth episode of a '60 Minutes' season has not drawn fewer than 7 million total viewers or 1 million in the key demographic since 2000. The show, which underwent a major overhaul under CBS News chief Bari Weiss, is now facing criticism for failing to improve its performance, with 'America's Funniest Home Videos' and 'The Price Is Right' outperforming it in the crucial 25-54 demographic. A veteran TV executive noted that the show's previous hosts, such as Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega, were well-regarded, and the current direction has reportedly made the show 'worse' in the eyes of viewers. item.title: Fox News viewership declines amid shifting political interests
item.description: Fox News is experiencing a significant drop in viewership, with October 2026 marking the network's lowest-rated month since December 2023, according to media newsletter Status. The decline is particularly pronounced among the 25-54 age demographic, which advertisers prioritize, with Fox News averaging just 98,000 viewers in this group—a 32% drop from the previous year. This represents the lowest-rated month for this demographic in 25 years. While Fox News still leads cable news overall, beating ESPN in total day viewership despite the return of football, the ratings decline is notable given the political context of the upcoming 2026 midterms. Weekday prime time shows hosted by Sean Hannity and Laura Ingraham are also seeing their lowest-rated months in both total viewers and the 25-54 demo since December 2023.
