item.description: The Supreme Court's conservative majority appears poised to potentially overturn a landmark 1990 ruling that has shaped religious freedom cases for decades. According to a CNN analysis cited in the article, the Court may deliver a significant victory for religious conservatives by revisiting Employment Division v. Smith, a decision written by the late Justice Antonin Scalia. The case in question, St. Mary Parish v. Roy, involves Catholic preschools and the Archdiocese of Denver seeking to participate in Colorado's universal preschool program without signing the state's nondiscrimination agreement covering sexual orientation and gender identity. A federal appeals court had previously ruled in favor of Colorado, relying on the Smith precedent which holds that neutral laws applicable to all do not require a 'compelling interest' to justify them. item.title: Jennifer Lopez Announces New Single 'Proof of Love' Amidst Vinyl Reissue of 2011 Album 'Love?'
item.description: Jennifer Lopez is preparing to release her new single 'Proof of Love,' which will serve as a bonus track on the first-ever vinyl edition of her 2011 album 'Love?,' set for release in November. The singer revealed that the song was inspired by the emotional transition her life underwent when her twins, Max and Emme Muniz, left for college. Lopez described the song as a 'happy dance song' that also addresses 'pain and grief when someone's gone,' emphasizing that the song aims to transform grief into a positive marker of love. She shared that the experience of her children leaving home prompted her to return to the studio, resulting in what she considers some of her best work to date. The 'Love?' vinyl reissue, which includes three different versions available for pre-order starting October 28, coincides with the premiere of her new concert film 'The JLo Show: Live in Vegas,' airing on CBS and Paramount+ on Thanksgiving night, November 26. item.description: The Washington Post reports on a new three-part Netflix documentary featuring Matthew Perry, the late 'Friends' star, which delves into his personal life and career struggles. The documentary, titled 'Matthew Perry: The Documentary,' includes interviews with Perry's close friends and family members who share intimate details about his battles with substance abuse throughout his adult life. The film begins with archival footage of Perry in his early 20s, struggling financially while waiting for his breakthrough role as Chandler Bing on 'Friends.' item.title: Trump's Louisiana Data Center Payment Claim Debunked by Local News Investigation
item.description: President Donald Trump made a false claim during a recent interview, stating that every resident living near a Louisiana data center received a $10,000 check. The claim was debunked by WWL-TV, a local New Orleans news station, which investigated the matter and found no evidence of such payments. item.title: SoFi Technologies Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Performance with $1.4 Billion in Revenue and $241 Million Net Income
item.description: SoFi Technologies, Inc. (SOFI) has reported its third quarter 2026 financial results, showcasing a record net revenue of $1.4 billion and net income of $241 million. The company's performance reflects significant growth across multiple business segments, with fee-based revenue reaching $1.429 billion for the quarter, up from $1.101 billion in the same period of 2025. Key drivers of this growth include strong performance in loan origination fees, technology services, and the newly launched SoFi Crypto platform. The company's loan origination fees increased to $607.6 million in Q3 2026 compared to $327.8 million in Q3 2025, while technology services revenue rose to $263.6 million from $151.7 million. The SoFi Crypto platform, launched in Q4 2025, contributed $3.7 million in net crypto transaction revenue during the quarter. SoFi's regulatory capital metrics also demonstrated strength, with CET1 risk-based capital at $9.52 billion, representing a 16.9% ratio against risk-weighted assets.

item.description: Democrats in Washington state have successfully turned the Republican strategy against them regarding a ballot measure targeting transgender athletes. This approach has united the party's progressive and moderate wings, with figures like Rep. Pramila Jayapal and Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez both opposing the measure. Jayapal emphasized using conservative values against them by highlighting the intrusion of government into family decisions. The opposition group No Hate in Washington State avoids using the term 'transgender' in ads, instead showing girls waiting for sex verification exams. item.title: GOP Consultant Identifies 'Red Scream' as Key Threat to Senate Majority in Upcoming Midterms
item.description: A veteran Republican consultant, Alex Castellanos, has introduced the term 'Red Scream' to describe growing frustration among conservatives and independents who feel ignored by Donald Trump and Republican leaders ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. According to an Axios report cited in the article, this frustration could lead to lower voter turnout among these groups, potentially costing Republicans control of the Senate. Castellanos emphasized that the 'Red Scream' represents a more significant concern than the anticipated 'blue wave' of Democratic voter enthusiasm. Senate Republicans are currently assessing their prospects in several key states, with Iowa appearing to favor them, Ohio showing signs of slipping, and Alaska and Kansas viewed with increasing pessimism. The report notes that top Republican operatives struggle to envision a Senate majority beyond 51 seats. item.description: Democrats are capitalizing on reported fractures within President Donald Trump's 'Make America Healthy Again' (MAHA) coalition, which has been a key component of his political base. The coalition, initially formed around promises to improve food safety and reduce harmful chemicals in the food supply, has faced internal disputes over the pace of policy changes, particularly regarding pesticide regulations. According to Axios, Trump's health adviser Calley Means resigned amid disagreements over the slow progress of food-policy reforms, with other MAHA leaders publicly criticizing the administration's handling of these issues. Vani Hari, known as Food Babe, accused Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. of being hindered by 'corporate capture and special interests' at the White House. item.title: TikTok Creators Monetize Copper Wire Stripping as a Side Hustle Amid Rising Prices
item.description: Copper prices have reached record highs, driving a surge in TikTok content where creators demonstrate stripping copper wire for resale. The trend, which has gained traction among diverse users including hobbyists, electricians, and teenagers, involves documenting the process of removing insulation from copper wire to sell the metal. According to the article, copper prices hit $14,473 per metric ton in September 2026, more than double the 2020 price, making scrap copper highly valuable. While some creators earn modest income from selling stripped copper, many generate significant revenue through TikTok Shop by promoting wire strippers and other tools. For example, one creator reported earning $1,446 from a video with 6.8 million views, while another sold over 20,000 wire strippers globally. item.title: The Institute of Housing and the Skin of Madrid: A Historical Reflection on Urban Development
item.description: The article discusses the historical context of housing policies in Spain, particularly under the Franco regime, and their lasting impact on urban development. It references the Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda (National Housing Institute) and its role in shaping residential areas, especially in Madrid. The author, Juan Manuel Grijalvo, explores how housing projects during Franco's era were designed to create a sense of stability and control, often displacing rural populations into urban outskirts. The text includes personal anecdotes from readers about living in neighborhoods built during this period, such as Colmenar Viejo, which were initially seen as undesirable but later became valuable due to their location. The discussion also touches on the political implications of housing policies, comparing the current state of public housing in areas governed by different political parties, such as PSOE and PP. item.title: GOP Claims Hidden Advantage in Senate Races Amid Democratic Missteps
item.description: The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) has been promoting a 'hidden advantage' for Republicans in the 2026 Senate races, claiming Democrats have made a 'huge mistake' by focusing too much on Texas while neglecting other traditionally Democratic states. In a fundraising email sent to donors, the NRSC criticized 'the Democrat media' for publishing polls showing Republican losses in Texas and accused outlets of 'gushing' over Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico's fundraising success. The email asserted that Republicans are 'SURGING in historically blue states!' and cited Minnesota as an example, claiming that Senate nominee Michele Tafoya is 'statistically TIED' with her Democratic opponent, though no specific poll was referenced. Hours later, former President Donald Trump amplified this message on Truth Social, endorsing Tafoya and warning that the only way she could lose is if Democrats 'cheat' by manipulating ballots. item.title: U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency Confirms China's Reusable Spaceplane in Satellite Image
item.description: The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that a satellite image circulating since 2024 depicts China's secretive reusable orbital spaceplane, resolving earlier uncertainty about its identity. The image, originally captured by Maxar Technologies (now Vantor), was first publicly shown in 2024 by U.S. Space Force Col. John Patrick during the Open Space Forum in South Korea. The DIA's 2026 report, 'Challenges to Security in Space 2026,' includes a higher-resolution version of the photograph, providing one of the clearest public views of China's experimental spacecraft. The report explicitly identifies the object as a Chinese spaceplane, noting its similarities to the American X-37B, an uncrewed reusable orbital vehicle operated by the U.S. Space Force. Both spacecraft feature compact shuttle-like fuselages, short wings, and twin vertical tails, though the Chinese vehicle appears to have longer wing chords. item.title: Egyptian court orders closure of independent news outlet Mada Masr and fines editor-in-chief
item.description: An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of Egypt's last remaining independent news outlets, and imposed a fine of three million Egyptian pounds ($53,400) on its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, for operating an unlicensed website. The New Cairo Misdemeanour Court also ordered the confiscation of the outlet's equipment and devices. Attalah was taken into custody following the ruling but was released hours later after Mada Masr paid the full fine. During her release procedures, Attalah learned she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website. Mada Masr's editorial criticized the court's actions, stating it entered court 'with a measure of faith in the law and the justice system' but found 'none of that faith intact.' item.title: Trump Banishes Bill Maher After Dinner Criticism, Echoes Soup Nazi Analogy
item.description: The article discusses a recent incident involving former U.S. President Donald Trump and comedian Bill Maher following a White House dinner. After Maher criticized Trump's low midterm approval ratings and mocked his behavior on his HBO show, Trump responded with a 1,300-word Truth Social post banning Maher from future dinners. The piece draws parallels between Trump's behavior and the 'Soup Nazi' character from Seinfeld, emphasizing Trump's demand for absolute loyalty at his dinners. The article notes that Maher was the second high-profile guest to face consequences for criticizing Trump, following former FBI Director James Comey, who was indicted multiple times after a 2017 dinner where Trump sought a loyalty pledge. The author argues that Trump's dinners function as a political echo chamber, inviting only those who offer unwavering support, such as Kanye West (Ye), Nick Fuentes, Kid Rock, and Stephen A. Smith. item.title: 1940s Brussels Street Life Captured in Vintage Photographs
item.description: The article presents a collection of 30 vintage photographs capturing everyday street life in Brussels during the 1940s. These images document pedestrians, shoppers, workers, and residents navigating the city's streets and squares throughout a decade marked by World War II occupation and postwar recovery. The photographs include specific locations such as Boulevard Adolphe Max and Boulevard Anspach, with dates ranging from March 1941 to October 1947. The images provide a historical record of urban life during the German occupation period (1940-1944) and the subsequent post-liberation era (1945-1947). The photographs show the subdued atmosphere of wartime Brussels alongside the renewed energy of the postwar period, offering a nostalgic glimpse into the city's daily movements and urban landscape more than eighty years ago. item.title: Women Athletes Face Higher Risk of Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S) with Subtle Early Symptoms
item.description: The article discusses Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S), a condition that occurs when athletes do not consume enough calories to meet the demands of their training or basic physiological needs. Women are at significantly higher risk than men, with a 2026 study in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport finding that 70% of high-level female athletes were at risk of developing RED-S. The condition can lead to a range of symptoms including fatigue, impaired concentration, frequent illnesses, poor recovery, irregular periods, weakened immune systems, and increased risk of injuries such as stress fractures. Early signs include persistent fatigue, longer recovery times after workouts, declining performance, more frequent illnesses, poor sleep, increased hunger, mood swings, hair loss, and weight loss. More serious symptoms include irregular or absent periods and frequent injuries. The article emphasizes that RED-S is not just about undereating but reflects chronic underfueling

item.title: Jio Platforms' stock surges 21% in debut following record-breaking Indian IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms, the Indian telecom and digital services unit owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani and backed by Meta and Google, experienced a 21% surge in its stock price during its market debut on Wednesday. The company raised $3.2 billion through India's largest and most subscribed initial public offering (IPO), which attracted over $77 billion in investor bids. The shares opened at ₹1,358 (approximately $14) per share, up from the IPO price of ₹1,119 ($12), valuing Jio Platforms at around ₹12.5 trillion ($131.9 billion). This makes it India's second-most valuable listed company after its parent Reliance Industries, which is valued at approximately ₹16 trillion ($168.6 billion). The IPO, which ran from October 21 to 22, saw bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer, with over 13.8 million applications, marking a record for the most subscribed stock offering in India. item.description: The Dallas Cowboys secured a crucial 38-21 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, ending a two-game losing streak and keeping pace with the 4-2-1 New York Giants in the NFC East. Quarterback Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, including two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens, while running back Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards, scoring the game-sealing touchdown with 2:21 remaining. The Cowboys' offense, which had struggled in recent games with only 29 combined points in their last two outings, showed significant improvement, marking the first time since 1983 that they achieved over 200 yards rushing and passing in a single game against the Eagles. item.title: Thunderbird: A Concept Space Station Designed Without Traditional Floors
item.description: The Thunderbird expandable space station, designed by OMI (Of My Imagination) in collaboration with Florida-based startup Max Space, represents a groundbreaking approach to space station architecture. Unlike traditional space stations that rely on gravity-defined floors, Thunderbird's interior design eliminates the concept of 'up' and 'down,' creating a circular layout where every surface can function as a floor. The station, which can be launched on a single SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, unfolds in orbit to approximately twenty times its folded size, providing 350 cubic meters of pressurized space—roughly a third of the International Space Station's volume. Its soft architecture, composed of layered fabric including Kevlar, meets or exceeds NASA safety standards for heat, vacuum, vibration, and micrometeoroid impacts. item.title: Federal Judge Rules LA's Top Prosecutor Unlawfully Serving, Bars Him from Two Cases
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli, Los Angeles' top federal prosecutor, is unlawfully serving in his position and has barred him from overseeing two criminal cases. Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright determined that the Justice Department had unlawfully delegated powers to Essayli, effectively making him a 'de facto' United States Attorney without proper Senate confirmation. The judge's ruling rejects the Justice Department's attempt to maintain Essayli's authority through a revised delegation of powers, stating that the revised arrangement made no meaningful difference as the powers in question could not have been lawfully delegated to him. Essayli, a former Republican California Assembly member, has been a key legal enforcer for the Trump administration, pursuing charges against protesters and activists while dropping cases involving administration allies. item.description: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has encouraged hecklers to continue shouting a specific phrase at President Donald Trump during his rallies. The incident occurred when a crowd member at a Trump rally in Mississippi yelled, 'Shove that ballroom up your fat ass!' during Trump's speech, prompting security to remove the individual. Kimmel, during his Tuesday night monologue, expressed hope that this phrase would become a recurring chant at Trump's events, joking that it would be 'a shame' if people started wearing shirts with the phrase. item.description: The article explores the growing 'sovereign baby' movement, where parents reject traditional medical systems and government documentation for their children. It highlights the deep distrust of medical institutions, particularly among women of color, who face systemic disparities in maternal care. The piece follows Sarah Ashley Townsend, whose mother refused hospital births and paperwork, leaving her without a birth certificate or Social Security number for most of her life. Townsend recounts the lifelong challenges she faced, including being denied a driver's license and struggling to secure her son's birth certificate due to her own lack of documentation. item.title: Pokémon Unite to Discontinue Switch Service in March 2027
item.description: Pokémon Unite, the free-to-play MOBA game developed by Tencent Games and published by The Pokémon Company, is set to end its service on the Nintendo Switch in March 2027. This announcement has been met with mixed reactions from the gaming community, with many players expressing disappointment over the game's monetization practices and the lack of alternatives for console players. The game, which launched on July 21, 2021, has faced criticism for its aggressive in-game purchases, including expensive cosmetic items like $40 skins for Pokémon characters. Players have noted that the game's monetization model has been a significant factor in its declining popularity, with many stating that the high costs discouraged regular play. item.title: Chiricahua Becomes America's 64th National Park, Celebrating Unique Geological Formations
item.description: Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona has been officially designated as America's 64th national park, marking the first new addition to the national park system in six years. Located in the Chiricahua Mountains, the park features a unique landscape of balanced rocks and rhyolite spires that have formed over millions of years. The area, known to the Apache people as 'the land of standing-up rocks,' covers approximately 12,000 acres of canyon country and includes hundreds of pinnacles that can reach up to hundreds of feet in height. The geological formations were created by volcanic activity approximately 27 million years ago, when the Turkey Creek eruption deposited vast amounts of ash that later cooled and fractured into columns. Over time, water erosion and freeze-thaw cycles shaped these columns into the distinctive spires seen today. item.title: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Calls for International Attention on Kashmir, Resource Management, and Energy Infrastructure
item.description: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Azar addressed the Karachi Press Club during a Meet the Press event, emphasizing the need for greater international focus on the region's constitutional status, natural resources, and economic challenges. He expressed concerns about the proposal to grant Gilgit-Baltistan provisional provincial status, stressing that the region's constitutional and political issues must be resolved before any such move. Azar criticized India's 2019 decision to revoke Jammu and Kashmir's special status, arguing that the international community has failed to take meaningful action against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He also highlighted the mismanagement of Gilgit-Baltistan's mineral resources, alleging that gold worth Rs15 billion is being extracted daily from the region. item.title: Elsa Lanchester's Early Career in 1920s London: Cabaret, Film, and Stage
item.description: Elsa Lanchester, the British actress later famous for her role as the Bride of Frankenstein, began her career in the late 1920s in London's vibrant bohemian scene. Before achieving Hollywood fame, she established herself as a multifaceted performer through cabaret ownership, music hall comedy, and early film roles. In the early 1920s, she co-founded and managed The Cave of Harmony, a popular London nightclub that became a hub for avant-garde artists and intellectuals including Evelyn Waugh, Christopher Isherwood, and Osbert Sitwell. Lanchester gained recognition for her satirical performances, often wearing top hats, tights, and high heels while performing cheeky, socially critical sketches and singing Victorian-era ballads. Her recordings, such as 'Please Sell No More Drink to My Father' (1926), were released on Columbia Records. item.title: Earwax's Dual Properties Offer Insights for Developing Natural Insect Repellents
item.description: Earwax, medically known as cerumen, has long been recognized for its role in ear health, but recent research reveals its unique physical properties could inspire safer insect repellents. Scientists from Georgia Institute of Technology conducted experiments observing how ants interact with earwax, discovering it possesses a paradoxical combination of slipperiness and stickiness. The study, published in the journal Soft Matter, found that earwax's structure—composed of skin flakes held together by a binder—creates a surface that ants struggle to navigate. When ants attempted to climb smooth earwax, they immediately fell due to the material's ability to absorb the moisture from their wet suction cups, preventing attachment. This dual property, known as shear-thinning, allows earwax to thin under physical deformation while maintaining its sticky nature. item.title: SK Hynix predicts memory shortages will continue through 2030 amid AI-driven demand
item.description: SK Hynix, a leading South Korean memory manufacturer, has forecasted that global memory shortages will persist until at least 2030, driven by surging demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure development. The company reported a significant quarterly revenue increase of ₩104.6 trillion ($78.1 billion), a 328 percent year-over-year growth, with operating profit reaching ₩87.68 trillion ($62.8 billion), up 486 percent annually. SK Hynix attributes this success to a 'virtuous cycle' where AI adoption drives increased infrastructure investment, which in turn fuels further AI development. The company noted that supply is not keeping pace with market growth due to technical challenges in leading-edge manufacturing processes and lengthy facility construction timelines. Despite planning to expand production capacity, SK Hynix acknowledged it cannot meet demand quickly enough, with 14 long-term contracts securing over half of its 2027-2028 output. item.title: Religious and racial divides shape Brazil's presidential election dynamics
item.description: Brazil's 2026 presidential election revealed deep political divisions rooted in religious and racial identities, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva securing a narrow victory over Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election highlighted how religious affiliations, particularly between Catholics and evangelicals, intersect with racial demographics. According to the article, 57% of Brazilians identify as Catholic and 27% as evangelical, reflecting a significant shift from three decades ago when 80% were Catholic. Evangelicals, who form a growing political force with nearly one-fifth of Brazil's Congress identifying as such, largely supported Flávio Bolsonaro, while Catholics tended to back Lula. item.title: Los Angeles sues celebrity dog rescue for operating as illegal business
item.description: The Los Angeles city attorney's office has filed a lawsuit against Wagmor Pets, an animal rescue organization once popular among Hollywood celebrities, alleging it operates as an illegal commercial enterprise. The lawsuit claims owner Melissa Bacelar purchased dogs from puppy mills and resold them to adopters at high prices, charging up to $1,500 per dog while falsely portraying them as rescued animals. City prosecutors state that Bacelar bought and resold 'hundreds if not thousands of dogs purchased from breeders,' with some dogs having serious health issues and dying shortly after purchase. The lawsuit seeks to bar Wagmor and Bacelar from fraudulent business practices and impose fines exceeding $7 million for violating city and state laws. item.title: Los Angeles Board Suspends Utility Shutoffs Amid Unusually High Bills
item.description: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (DWP) board has suspended residential water and electricity service shutoffs for nonpayment through the end of the year following a period of unusually high utility bills. The board, which does not have the authority to forgive the charges, encouraged residents to enroll in programs that could help alleviate rising costs. The move comes as complaints about unexpectedly high bills have spread widely on social media, with residents describing bills as 'outrageous,' 'insane,' and 'extremely crazy.' item.description: In a significant political development, Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) has endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins for governor of Alaska, effectively undermining President Donald Trump's preferred candidate, Bernadette Wilson, just one week before Election Day. The endorsement, reported by NBC News, comes as a surprise given Murkowski's history of clashing with Trump and her previous support for other Republican candidates. item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli, a United States Attorney for the Central District of California, is disqualified from overseeing several cases due to his improper appointment and ethical concerns. item.description: Right-wing podcaster Candace Owens has expressed satisfaction over a recent court decision that removed her personally from a defamation lawsuit filed by French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte Macron. The Delaware Superior Court judge, Sheldon K. Rennie, ruled that the court lacked jurisdiction over Owens, who resides in Tennessee, and dismissed all claims against her individually. item.description: The Justice Department has filed a memorandum in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia requesting that records related to the search of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's Washington home remain under seal. Federal prosecutors, led by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro and Associate Deputy Attorney General Alessandra Serano, argued that releasing even redacted versions of the warrant and supporting documents would jeopardize a 'complex investigation.' item.description: A federal investigation into two former FBI officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, has faced significant scrutiny following testimony from FBI agent Brian Witt. item.description: Thousands of voters in North Carolina, a key battleground state for the 2026 midterms, are encountering significant issues with their mail-in ballots due to a new Republican-imposed requirement that the inner ballot envelope must be completely sealed inside the outer envelope. item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an appeal with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit following a federal judge's decision to block President Donald Trump's plans for renovating East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction that prohibits the Trump administration from removing or damaging additional trees at the course and requires 10 business days' written notice before any irreversible changes to East Potomac Park. Judge Reyes' ruling cited Trump's own Truth Social posts, which contradicted sworn testimony from government employees and arguments made by Justice Department attorneys. item.title: Apple releases iOS 27.2 update featuring expanded Siri AI language support and security enhancements
item.description: Apple has released iOS 27.2 for iPhones and iPads, introducing expanded language support for Siri AI in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, with the ability to remember details from past conversations. The update also includes improved memory functions for Siri, allowing it to tap into sources like photos in Messages, calendar events, voicemails, Safari history, and reading lists. item.description: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter expressed strong skepticism toward the Trump administration's Justice Department during a court hearing regarding an emergency request to halt California from counting mail ballots from over 20,000 registered voters. The lawsuit claims Jennings ignored a retraction demand and kept the misleading content online. Piker's legal claims include defamation per se, defamation by implication, and false light, with $27.5 million in compensatory and $45 million in punitive damages sought. item.title: 1953 Chevrolet Corvette: The First American Sports Car Model
item.description: The 1953 Chevrolet Corvette marked the beginning of one of the most iconic American sports cars. Unveiled as a concept at the 1953 GM Motorama in New York, it entered limited production later that year with only 300 hand-built examples completed in Flint, Michigan. Every 1953 Corvette was finished in Polo White with a red interior and powered by a 150-horsepower "Blue Flame" inline-six engine paired exclusively with a two-speed Powerglide automatic transmission. Featuring a groundbreaking fiberglass body, the car combined sleek European-inspired styling with American engineering. Though production was modest and performance modest by later standards, the 1953 model established the Corvette name and laid the foundation for decades of legendary sports cars to follow. These classic photos capture the pioneering style and historic significance of the 1953 Chevrolet Corvette, the first of its kind. item.description: Sony has paid a security researcher $50,000 through its HackerOne bug bounty program for reporting a critical PlayStation 5 hypervisor exploit discovered with the help of generative AI. The researcher, known as Jordy, confirmed the payout and explained that he initially agreed not to report the bug but changed his decision after learning that another person had found the same vulnerability using AI tools. The exploit affects PS5 firmware versions 13.60 through 14.00, allowing kernel-level access to run unsigned code or boot Linux. item.title: Satellite data confirms AMOC weakening trend over 30 years
item.description: Satellite measurements have provided some of the strongest evidence yet that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), a crucial ocean current system that transports warm water from the Gulf of Mexico to the North Atlantic, is weakening. According to research published in New Scientist, the AMOC has slowed by 14 percent over a 30-year period, based on analysis of heat flux from the ocean to the atmosphere. The study, led by Richard Allan of the University of Reading, UK, used satellite data to measure how much heat the North Atlantic is releasing into the atmosphere, finding an 18 percent decrease in heat flux over 40 years. This decline in heat release correlates with the AMOC's reduced ability to transport warm water northward, which helps maintain Europe's relatively mild climate. item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to revive deportation cases previously closed under Biden policy
item.description: The Supreme Court has issued a significant ruling that impacts immigration policy, allowing the Trump administration to potentially reopen thousands of deportation cases that were previously closed under a Biden-era policy. The conservative-majority court cleared the way for the Trump administration to restrict a policy known as 'administrative closure,' which permitted immigration judges to set aside cases without formally dismissing them. This practice, used for decades, has allowed approximately 360,000 migrants to have their cases closed since 1990, providing relief to those with strong claims to remain in the U.S., such as victims of crime or neglected children. The Biden administration formalized this practice in 2024 through regulation, but the Trump administration, upon returning to power, withdrew its defense of the policy. item.title: Book alleges UAE paid Kushner $50M to remove Tillerson from Trump administration
item.description: A new book by Matthew Cole titled 'Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed's Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East' has sparked controversy with allegations that the United Arab Emirates paid Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law, $50 million to help oust then-Secretary of State Rex Tillerson. According to The New Republic, the book claims that Tillerson had become 'extremely cozy with the Qataris' and opposed the Saudi- and Emirati-led blockade of Qatar during his 2017-2018 tenure. Both Gulf nations lobbied for Tillerson's removal, and Trump fired him on Twitter in March 2018. The book states that Kushner had quietly pushed for Tillerson's exit for months and urged UAE leader Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to 'speed up their agreed-upon payment.' The book alleges that $50 million was routed through Azerbaijan to a Cyprus bank account for Kushner a month later. item.title: FBI Searches Mansion of Swalwell Backer Amid Congressional Investigation
item.description: FBI agents conducted a search of billionaire Stephen Cloobeck's Beverly Hills mansion on Tuesday as part of a federal investigation into former Democratic Congressman Eric Swalwell. Cloobeck, a former supporter of Swalwell who later became a vocal critic, had previously described Congress as 'a cesspool' and urged journalists to 'start investigating everyone in Congress' after multiple women accused Swalwell of sexual misconduct. The search, which occurred one week before the November 3 midterms, was part of an ongoing probe into Swalwell, though officials stated no arrests were expected at the residence. Cloobeck, a hospitality mogul who ended his own gubernatorial bid to support Swalwell's campaign, turned against the congressman after the allegations surfaced. He told FOX 11 in April that Swalwell 'never brought a woman' to his mansion and expressed disappointment with Democrats, declaring himself a Republican. item.title: Medieval Bookmarks: Practical Tools for Manuscript Readers
item.description: The article explores the history and variety of medieval bookmarks, which were practical tools used by readers to mark their place in manuscripts. Unlike modern decorative bookmarks, medieval bookmarks were functional and often made from available materials. The author, Jenneka Janzen, identifies three main types of medieval bookmarks: fore-edge bookmarks, register bookmarks, and found object bookmarks. Fore-edge bookmarks consisted of tabs made from parchment, leather, or woven beads, stitched or looped into the page at the desired text location. These were commonly found in liturgical books, helping readers locate specific readings during religious services. Register bookmarks resembled modern bookmarks and came in three variations: simple strips attached to the book's endband, portable versions with strings attached to an anchor, and a sophisticated rotating dial system that indicated column positions in multi-column texts. item.title: FBI raids Beverly Hills mansion linked to Eric Swalwell donor amid federal investigation
item.description: The FBI conducted a raid on a Beverly Hills mansion believed to belong to billionaire Stephen Cloobeck, a former donor and political ally of California Democratic politician Eric Swalwell, according to reports from Fox News and CNN. The search, which took place on Tuesday morning, is part of a federal investigation into Swalwell, who resigned from Congress and dropped out of the California gubernatorial race in April following allegations of sexual misconduct. item.description: Vice President JD Vance confronted reporters at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, on October 27, 2026, during a press briefing before traveling to Michigan for a midterm election rally. Vance criticized the media for allegedly failing to scrutinize Democratic tactics in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, where he claimed there was 'electoral fraud' due to ballot confusion between two candidates named Dan Sullivan. He argued that placing a candidate with a similar name to an incumbent on the ballot was misleading, stating, 'When you put a person on the ballot explicitly to try to confuse voters, I think that's the definition of electoral fraud.' Vance then shifted focus to the press, accusing them of not holding Democrats accountable and urging them to 'do your job' by questioning the Democratic Party's strategy. item.title: FBI Whistleblower Warns Rush to Release Epstein Files Could Harm Victims and Staff
item.description: An FBI whistleblower raised concerns about Director Kash Patel's rushed release of Jeffrey Epstein's files, warning that the process could 'destroy people's lives' due to potential errors. The internal complaint, filed in March 2025 by an unnamed official in the FBI's Information Management Division, alleged that Patel threatened to fire staff if deadlines were not met. The whistleblower feared the rushed timeline would lead to mistakes that could expose agents' identities and victim details, potentially making them targets. The complaint also suggested Patel's deadline might serve as a pretext for staff cuts, with employees being scapegoated for procedural failures. The FBI's Office of Integrity and Compliance referred the complaint to the Justice Department's inspector general, though no further action was confirmed. item.title: Nanette Fabray: A Look at Her Iconic 1950s Career Through Rare Photos
item.description: Nanette Fabray (October 27, 1920 – February 22, 2018) was an American actress, singer, and dancer who reached the peak of her mainstream fame during the 1950s. Transitioning seamlessly from Broadway to television and film, Fabray became a household name through her work on 'Caesar's Hour' (1954–1957), where she served as Sid Caesar's main comedic partner. Her exceptional sketch comedy timing and musical talents earned her three Emmy Awards during her tenure on the show. She unexpectedly left the series in 1956 due to a contractual misunderstanding between her business manager and Caesar, a conflict that took years to resolve. Fabray also starred in the critically acclaimed musical film 'The Band Wagon' (1953), where she played Lily Marton, a character inspired by Broadway legend Betty Comden. item.title: Chinese Scientists Uncover 'D-rex,' a Fungus Evolving Since Dinosaur Extinction
item.description: Chinese scientists have identified a new species of fungus, Dianjunus rex, which they've nicknamed 'D-rex,' that represents the largest known ascomycete fruiting body. The fungus, discovered in Yunnan Province, China, can grow up to 50 cm (20 inches) tall and weigh nearly 5 pounds, significantly larger than previous records. Its evolutionary lineage dates back approximately 65 million years, coinciding with the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event that wiped out non-avian dinosaurs. Researchers from the Kunming Institute of Botany established that this fungus belongs to a new family, Dianjunaceae, within the order Xylariales. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about fungal size limits and suggests that environmental changes following the dinosaur extinction may have facilitated its evolution. The fungus produces unique reproductive structures called stromata that emerge from the roots of Chinese cork oak trees. Genetic analysis revealed that D-rex's closest relative is Grap

item.title: Raw Story to Offer Free Midterm Election Coverage on Election Day
item.description: Raw Story, an independent news outlet, has announced that it will provide free access to all of its 2026 midterm election coverage for 24 hours on Tuesday, November 3rd. The decision comes as Americans prepare to head to the polls in an election that will determine the direction of the country for years to come. The stakes are high, with control of Congress at risk and voters making critical decisions about leaders who will shape laws, protect rights, and hold power accountable. Raw Story's Editor-in-Chief, Adam Nichols, explained that the company believes every American deserves access to reliable, independent journalism to understand what's happening and what's at stake. The news organization will remove subscription restrictions from all midterm election stories, including breaking news, original reporting, in-depth investigations, commentary, analysis, and a live election blog. item.title: U.S. Attorney's Office Revises Claims Against FBI Officials Hours Before Court Hearing
item.description: The U.S. Attorney's office for Washington, D.C., led by Jeanine Pirro, has revised its legal claims against two former FBI officials just hours before a scheduled court hearing. The revised affidavit, filed at 12:22 a.m. on Tuesday, replaces the original version that had accused Nicole Floris and Bradley Benavides of lying to Congress about the FBI's handling of the Hunter Biden investigation. The original affidavit, sworn by FBI Special Agent Byron Militello on October 20, claimed that FBI Employee 1 was the primary conduit between the Criminal Division and the Foreign Influence Task Force, stating that the FBI had possession of Hunter Biden's laptop and that it belonged to him. The revised version, signed by FBI Special Agent Bryan Witt with blank lines for signature and date, alters key language, describing FBI Employee 1 as 'one of the primary conduits' rather than 'the primary conduit,' and changes 'the lead agent overseeing' to 'an agent involved in overseeing.' item.title: Israeli Military Chief Defies Netanyahu Over Election-Eve Iran Operation Plan
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a close ally of former U.S. President Donald Trump, is facing an unprecedented internal conflict within Israel's military leadership regarding a planned military operation that officials fear could provoke a confrontation with Iran just days before the upcoming elections. According to Channel 12's Yaron Avraham, Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir refused to execute the operation without a written legal authorization and a thorough discussion with political leadership, marking a rare public stand against Netanyahu's government. Zamir, who was previously seen as a loyal supporter of Netanyahu, reportedly stood alone in his objections, with Mossad and Shin Bet heads reportedly backing the operation. Recent polls indicate Netanyahu's rival, former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot, is leading in the polls. item.title: Defense Secretary Hegseth's Masculinity Image Fails to Resonate with Americans in Poll
item.description: A recent YouGov poll conducted for The Bulwark and the podcast 'Pablo Torre Finds Out' reveals that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is widely viewed as a poor role model for American men. The survey, which polled 1,417 adults between October 10 and 14 with a margin of error of ±3.6 percentage points, found that only 28% of American adults consider Hegseth a strong role model for men, while 39% disagree. Among younger adults aged 18-29, the disapproval rate is even higher, with just 18% viewing him positively compared to 34% who do not. The poll highlights Hegseth's 'alpha male preening' as a key factor in his low approval ratings, noting his efforts to project a masculine image through various initiatives including rebranding the Pentagon as the Department of War, requiring testosterone screenings for service members, posting workout videos with troops, mocking overweight individuals as 'fatties,' and expressing skepticism toward women in leadership roles. item.title: Aaron Sorkin Reflects on Directing Challenges, 'The West Wing' Revival, and Revisiting 'A Few Good Men'
item.description: Aaron Sorkin, renowned screenwriter and director, recently discussed his experiences with directing during an appearance at the Newport Beach Film Festival. Sorkin, who received the Maverick Director Award for his film 'The Social Reckoning,' candidly admitted he was his second choice to direct the film, preferring David Fincher, who has an exclusive Netflix deal. The film, which explores Facebook's harmful effects and a whistleblower's role, has underperformed compared to his earlier work 'The Social Network,' with only $15 million in worldwide gross and a 54% Rotten Tomatoes rating. Sorkin, with a 35-year career in screenwriting, acknowledged his struggles with directing, particularly in visual storytelling and camera work, stating, 'I have no visual sensibility, it turns out.' item.description: A recent report by independent journalist Ken Klippenstein, citing three officials with knowledge of internal discussions, has revealed that the Justice Department (DOJ) has been developing contingency plans to potentially intervene in the upcoming midterm elections. The report details 'doomsday' scenarios that include foreign cyberattacks and polling chaos, though officials describe these as improbable but not impossible. The administration has already hinted at such actions, with Attorney General Todd Blanche refusing to rule out blocking a state from certifying election results in a 'doomsday scenario.' The DOJ has also sought court intervention to halt certification in Alaska's Senate race if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses. The report draws parallels to the 2020 election, with a government lawyer noting that Trump-aligned lawyers are expected to amplify claims of impropriety post-election. item.title: Former DHS Official Reports $377 Billion in Alleged Corruption During Trump's Second Term
item.description: A former Department of Homeland Security chief of staff, Miles Taylor, has released a detailed report and documentary titled 'Corruptionland' that alleges approximately $377 billion in corruption tied to President Donald Trump's second administration. Taylor, a prominent critic of Trump, stated that no one in Washington had previously attempted to quantify the total amount of alleged wrongdoing, so his team reviewed 100 cases of alleged misconduct since Trump's reelection. The report combines public funds, private benefits, and the dollar value of transactions linked to these cases, though Taylor noted that over half of the cases (59) could not be assigned a monetary value due to the nature of the alleged misconduct, such as firing inspectors general or imprisoning critics. The report also excludes the economic impact of Trump's tariffs, which Taylor described as impossible to measure. item.description: At a political rally in Montana, Vice President JD Vance made a comment about rising gas prices that inadvertently highlighted the connection between President Donald Trump's foreign policy and economic consequences. Vance attempted to explain high gas prices as temporary disruptions caused by external factors, citing historical examples like the 1979 Iran hostage crisis, the 2001 terrorist attacks, and the 2007 financial crisis. He stated, 'They skyrocket every time some tinpot dictator decides to throw a tantrum,' which many interpreted as a veiled reference to Trump's recent military actions in Iran. The remark quickly drew criticism and mockery online, with social media users pointing out the irony of Vance's words. item.title: Jean-Luc Godard Arrested During 1968 Paris Student Protests While Documenting Social Unrest
item.description: During the May 1968 protests in Paris, French New Wave filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard was detained by police while filming student demonstrations. The unrest began as student protests against government authority and educational institutions, quickly escalating into a nationwide movement involving over 10 million workers who joined general strikes and occupied factories. Godard, deeply engaged in the political climate, documented the clashes between students, workers, and law enforcement. Just days before his arrest, Godard and fellow director François Truffaut shut down the 1968 Cannes Film Festival by physically blocking screenings, declaring it inappropriate to discuss film techniques during a national crisis. His arrest marked a turning point in his career, leading him to abandon conventional narrative cinema. item.title: Texas Governor's Secret Meeting with Big Tech Backfires as Data Center Opposition Grows
item.description: Texas Governor Greg Abbott, a prominent MAGA figure, is facing growing backlash over a closed-door meeting held with major technology companies in December 2025. The meeting, attended by representatives from Google, OpenAI, Meta, Amazon Web Services, and Nvidia, along with state electricity regulators and transmission companies, was intended to reassure Big Tech that Texas would support their data center projects. According to newly obtained records and interviews, Abbott's staff assured the tech companies that the state would help clear regulatory obstacles for their projects. Two days after the meeting, the state's grid manager, ERCOT, introduced a fast-track process for connecting data centers to the grid, which closely mirrored a proposal submitted by Google and another data center developer. item.title: El ascensor: cómo transformó la arquitectura y las jerarquías sociales en el siglo XX
item.description: El ascensor, un invento que ha existido desde hace aproximadamente dos mil años en formas primitivas, pero que se popularizó con el diseño del freno de seguridad de Elisha Otis en el siglo XIX, ha tenido un impacto profundo en la estructura social y arquitectónica de las ciudades. La noticia relata cómo el zar Nicolás II de Rusia se negó a usar el ascensor en el hotel Adlon de Berlín en 1913, prefiriendo que se vaciara la segunda planta para alojar a su séquito en lugar de utilizar el ascensor. Este incidente refleja una resistencia más amplia de la aristocracia europea hacia el ascensor, no por miedo o protocolo, sino porque consideraban que el ascensor era un artefacto democrático que amenazaba su estatus jerárquico. Antes del ascensor, la arquitectura reflejaba claramente las jerarquías sociales: las plantas más altas eran para los sirvientes y los pobres, mientras que las más bajas eran para los nobles. item.title: Elizaveta Tuktamysheva reflexiona sobre el miedo al hielo y los costes de la perfección en el patinaje artístico
item.description: Elizaveta Tuktamysheva, campeona del mundo y de Europa de patinaje artístico, ha compartido en una entrevista con la periodista rusa Irina Shikhman detalles sobre su trayectoria y los desafíos que enfrentó durante su carrera. La patinadora, quien ganó títulos internacionales, reconoció que necesitó toda una carrera para sentirse cómoda en la pista sin miedo. En la conversación, abordó temas como la violencia en los entrenamientos, los problemas alimentarios y el uso de laxantes para controlar el peso, así como el acoso que sufrió en 2025. Tuktamysheva explicó que desde pequeña, a los nueve años, viajó a San Petersburgo con su entrenador, lo que marcó un cambio en su infancia, convirtiéndola en 'un robot que simplemente ejecutaba lo que le ordenaban'. Recordó el miedo que sentía al pisar el hielo, aunque no podía precisar qué temía exactamente, y cómo aprendió a no expresar sus emociones para evitar represalias. item.title: El proyecto fotográfico Documerica retrató la vida cotidiana y los efectos de la contaminación en Estados Unidos durante los años 70
item.description:
Una colección de fotografías en color de la década de 1970 ofrece una visión de la vida cotidiana en Estados Unidos y de los problemas medioambientales que afectaban a numerosas comunidades. Las imágenes forman parte de Documerica, un proyecto impulsado por la Agencia de Protección Ambiental estadounidense (EPA) a principios de los años setenta para documentar las condiciones ambientales del país y las consecuencias de la actividad industrial.
Las fotografías muestran situaciones especialmente preocupantes. En Ruston, Washington, Gene Daniels retrató en agosto de 1972 a unos niños jugando en el patio de una vivienda mientras una fundición de Tacoma dispersaba residuos de arsénico y plomo sobre la zona. En Birmingham, Alabama, Leroy Woodson documentó viviendas próximas a una planta de tuberías de U.S. Steel, rodeadas de un intenso smog industrial. item.title: Miguel, que lleva cuatro años durmiendo en su coche para financiar la residencia de su madre de 95 años, obtiene vivienda social
item.description: Miguel, un hombre mallorquín de 95 años de edad, ha conseguido una vivienda social del Institut Balear de l'Habitatge (Ibavi) tras pasar cuatro años durmiendo en su vehículo para poder contribuir al pago de la residencia de su madre, quien tiene 95 años y requiere atención permanente. El caso, que se hizo público gracias a la mediación de Rubén Díaz, un activista que difundió la historia en redes sociales, revela una situación de gran dificultad económica y personal. Miguel, que padece cáncer de próstata con metástasis en los huesos y una infección pulmonar, recibe una pensión de 800 euros mensuales, mientras que el coste de la residencia de su madre asciende a 2.200 euros al mes. Para afrontar este gasto, la familia alquiló el piso propiedad de la madre y complementó el importe con parte de la jubilación de Miguel. item.title: Valencia limitará a diez personas los grupos turísticos en bicicleta y VMP para mejorar la movilidad urbana
item.description: El Ayuntamiento de Valencia ha anunciado una propuesta para limitar a un máximo de diez personas los grupos turísticos que circulen en bicicleta o vehículos de movilidad personal (VMP) por la ciudad. La concejala de Innovación, Turismo e Inversiones, Paula Llobet, presentó esta medida durante la Mesa de Diálogo y Turismo, destacando que busca reducir las quejas vecinales y garantizar una movilidad más ordenada y segura. La propuesta, que se incorporará como modificación a la Ordenanza de Movilidad, establece que los grupos que superen el límite de diez personas deberán fraccionarse en subgrupos de máximo diez, manteniendo una distancia mínima de 50 metros entre ellos. Esta regulación representa una reducción respecto al límite anterior, que permitía grupos de hasta 15 personas, y se adapta a las características de la red viaria y ciclista de Valencia. item.title: Iron Maiden homenajea a Samuel Taylor Coleridge con «Rime of the Ancient Mariner» en Powerslave
item.description: La noticia analiza la canción «Rime of the Ancient Mariner» de Iron Maiden, incluida en el álbum Powerslave de 1984, que celebra su 36º aniversario el 4 de septiembre de 2020. La canción, inspirada en el poema homónimo de Samuel Taylor Coleridge (1798), es considerada por el autor como la canción perfecta de la banda. El artículo explica que Powerslave fue grabado durante la gira de Piece of Mind, con una formación estable de la banda que marcó sus mejores años. La canción, de 13 minutos y 49 segundos, es la más larga de Iron Maiden hasta la publicación de Book of Souls en 2015. Su estructura musical refleja el poema romántico, con un galopante inicio que evoca la épica narrativa, seguido de cambios de ritmo que transmiten la desesperación de los marineros en la travesía. La letra sigue fielmente el relato del poema, donde un marinero mata un albatros, provocando una maldición que lleva a la tripulación a la desesperación y a la muerte. item.title: Subdirector de Adif condenado a indemnizar a trabajador por represalia laboral
item.description: La sentencia reciente en el caso de Adif, empresa pública dependiente del Ministerio de Transportes, ha establecido un precedente importante en el ámbito laboral. Un subdirector de circulación noroeste de Adif, identificado como Máximo de Hacendado en la noticia, ha sido condenado a pagar 7.501 euros a un trabajador por vulnerar su derecho fundamental a la libertad de expresión. El conflicto surgió cuando el trabajador, un técnico de gestión con siete años de antigüedad, publicó en redes sociales una queja sobre la falta de formación en su puesto. Como represalia, el subdirector le retiró dos de los tres días de teletrabajo que tenía asignados, acompañando sus palabras con comentarios despectivos y lenguaje malsonante. El trabajador grabó la reunión de confrontación, lo que constituyó una prueba clave para su demanda. item.title: Jesús de Miguel fallece tras accidente en partido de fútbol contra el Andorra
item.description: El club de fútbol CD Tenerife ha comunicado el fallecimiento del jugador Jesús de Miguel Alameda, ocurrido este martes 3 de noviembre de 2026, a las 8:00 horas. El futbolista, de 24 años, sufrió un grave accidente durante el partido contra el FC Andorra disputado el lunes 2 de noviembre en el estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López. Durante el encuentro, en el minuto 108, Jesús de Miguel colisionó con el portero visitante Jesús Owono en una disputa por un balón dividido. El impacto fue tan fuerte que obligó a suspender el partido de manera definitiva para permitir la atención médica inmediata. El jugador permaneció en observación en el Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, donde se informó que su condición médica había empeorado neurológicamente. El club confirmó a las 8:00 horas del martes que Jesús de Miguel había fallecido. item.title: Palantir lanza chaqueta de estilo workwear como símbolo de identidad tecnológica y apoyo a instituciones occidentales
item.description: Palantir, empresa de análisis de datos conocida por sus contratos militares y migratorios, ha lanzado una línea de ropa que busca convertir su identidad tecnológica en una señal de pertenencia cultural. El producto estrella es una chaqueta de algodón tipo chore coat, disponible en azul intenso y negro con un pequeño logo de Palantir en el bolsillo, que se agotó el mismo día de su lanzamiento tras producirse solo 420 unidades. La compañía, fundada por Alex Karp, ha pasado de ser una empresa de análisis de datos a ser un símbolo entre sectores conservadores tras publicar un manifiesto que afirma que 'la IA militar es inevitable, el poder blando ya no basta'. La chaqueta, vendida a 239 dólares, representa una estrategia para identificar a una comunidad de seguidores que comparten sus ideas sobre el futuro de la tecnología, más allá de sus clientes institucionales.
